Over-smoothing represents a critical barrier in Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs), causing graph node labels to converge as training progresses. In this study, we offer a rigorous upper limit on the separation between node labels, demonstrating that this separation diminishes when specific conditions regarding weight matrices, convolutional polynomials, and graph spectral properties are met. Consequently, our findings provide theoretical justification for a previously observed phenomenon: the process of over-smoothing is heavily contingent on how graph weights are normalized during convolution operations.

This study details a search for dark matter involving Z boson associated production conducted by the CMS experiment at the CERN proton-proton collider during 2017–2018. Data were gathered across 35.9 fb$^{-1}$ of integrated luminosity at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV. The analysis targets final states characterized by high transverse momentum leptons (electrons or muons) paired with significant missing transverse momentum. The dataset was partitioned into eight distinct categories based on lepton type, charge, and jet multiplicity. Signal yields were derived using template fitting methods applied to the distribution of the variable mT, defined as the transverse mass between the lepton and the hypothesized dark matter particle. Analysis results constrain the cross sections for dark matter production in linked processes with Z bosons, with limits reaching up to 10 pb. These findings are contrasted against Standard Model predictions and existing CMS limits. The study further establishes new constraints on simplified models featuring dark matter coupled to the Standard Model via Z bosons, Higgs bosons, or W bosons, as well as presenting novel limits on compressed supersymionic scenarios involving the decay of leptophilic squarks into leptons and neutralinos.

We demonstrate that the gauge links within global (schemes) parton distribution functions (PDFs) and the light-front wave function definitions of the parton distribution asymmetry $x$ and the transverse momentum asymmetry $x$ are not arbitrary. Instead, they are dictated by the associated parton distribution functions (PDFs) themselves. Specifically, we examine how the intrinsic transverse momentum ($k_\perp$) relates to the gauge links in both TMD PDFs and qTMD PDFs. Our findings show that the gauge links are determined by the magnitude of $k_\perp$ and exhibit a universal structure independent of the parton flavor, although different flavors may have varying magnitudes. This insight offers fresh perspectives on interpreting physical meanings of momentum scales and the gauge links, thereby enabling more rigorous analyses of their interrelationships.

A topological group is defined as the limit of a directed system (colimit) involving "spaces with socks." In this context, each component is the product of a T₀-group and the interval [0,1], equipped with the standard topology. This paper extends the work presented in [1] by exploring how the properties of the individual spaces influence the resulting topological group. Specifically, we demonstrate that a topological group G is the long product (colimit) of second-countable groups with the weak topology if and only if G is locally compact and Hausdorff. Furthermore, we show that G is the long product (colimit) of uncountable-dimensional groups endowed with the weak topology precisely when G is both compact and Hausdorff. Finally, we prove that G is the long product (colimit) of homogeneous spaces, equipped with the weak topology if and only if G is the interval [0,1].

Remote epitaxy enables growing high-quality crystals on substrates that are not in direct contact with the target material, utilizing an intermediary layer. However, this process often suffers from the emergence of pinhole epitaxy due to lattice mismatch. To mitigate this, we utilized Heusler compounds—specifically Co₂MnSi, Co₂MnSb, and Co₂FeSi—on graphene/sapphire. The CO₂MnSi and Co₂MnSb layers exhibited both remote and pinhole epitaxial growth, whereas Co₂FeSi displayed pure remote epitaxy. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations revealed that Co₂FeSi possesses the most accurate pseudomatching lattice constant to CO₂, facilitating a single orientation for epitaxial growth, while the other two Heuslers show multiple orientations. Consequently, the study identifies remote epitaxy as the most reliable method for growing high-quality Co₂MnSi and Co₂MnSb films, while also mapping the remote epitaxial lattice space across various Heusler materials on graphene/sapphire.

This paper proposes a new class of multivariate heavy-tailed non-stationary time series models designed to capture complex dependencies found in real-world data. We develop the necessary theory for this class and present novel statistical inference methods, specifically a non-parametric cross-spectral estimation technique and an innovative method for selecting the number of frequencies. Furthermore, we introduce a Bayesian approach capable of estimating model parameters, heavy-tail parameters, and time-varying spectral characteristics, supported by consistent estimation results. Finally, we validate our methods through simulations and an analysis of real-world datasets.

The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has identified a red supergiant (RSG) star at a distance of 295 Mpc within the massive galaxy cluster ACT-CL J0102−4915 (Ero-Saurus), also known as "El Gordo." This object, designated JWST-RSG1, exhibits a luminosity of $L = 1.7 \times 10^5 L_\odot$ and an effective temperature of $T_{\rm eff} = 3200$ K, corresponding to a mass of $M = 15 M_\odot$. It is the first RSG confirmed at such cosmological distances. Although JWST-RSG1 is physically small, it appears significantly brighter than other sources in the $[10.5]$ and $[11.2]$ bands due to strong thermal emission from dust in its circumstellar envelope. Consequently, it was initially mistaken for a distant galaxy; however, its spectral features, including PAH emission and molecular bands, confirm its stellar nature. Furthermore, the study demonstrates that JWST-RSG1 is a gravitationally lensed RSG, with a magnification factor of $\mu = 1.6^{+0.4}_{-0.3}$.

Streaming video platforms, such as Netflix and YouTube, contend with rising user demands for content volume and quality, which often strain network resources and lead to subpar user experiences. To address this, we propose a profit-sharing framework wherein content providers compensate service providers to purchase network capacity upgrades. First, we model the strategic interaction between a service provider and a content provider as a Stackelberg game to model their negotiation dynamics. Subsequently, we examine a scenario where multiple content and service providers operate within the network, analyzing the resulting equilibrium outcomes regarding network investments, data traffic levels, and earnings for both parties. Finally, we evaluate how varying user valuation thresholds for network performance influence the optimal design of these sharing agreements.

This work outlines the construction of a pair of adjunctions involving categories of observables and states on one side, and (compact) C*-algebras and (compact) statistical states on the other. Specifically, the functor mapping a state-space adjunction into one linking (compactly generated) C*-algebras and (compactly generated) statistical states is fully faithful.

$\alpha$-attractor models have emerged as a prominent class of single-field inflationary frameworks. This study reviews various $\alpha$-attractor architectures, including those derived from supergravity, quaternionic geometry, and two-field systems projected onto their $\alpha$-attractor components. Additionally, we provide the predicted values for scalar and tensor spectral indices, along with the ratio of their amplitudes. Finally, we outline the predictions regarding non-Gaussianity and establish the conditions under which these models predict a slowing-down or acceleration of the inflationary expansion.

We demonstrate that a quasi-Fuchsian surface forms a neighborhood of the Fuchsian form possesses a measured foliation at infinity, provided it is sufficiently close to said Fuchsian form. This extends the discovery made by Otal, who identified such structures in the limit set of real-analytic quasi-Fuchsian surfaces. The demonstration relies on a $C^1$-structural stability argument, which leverages a recent $C^1$-asymptotic compactness theorem by Bonifant and the author.

This study examines the distribution of return cross-sections across time for a broad spectrum of investment portfolios. Our findings indicate that, under a zero-mean assumption, the distribution approximates a Gaussian distribution with heteroscedastic variance. We further demonstrate how this distributional property drives key financial outcomes, specifically by explaining the time-series distribution of the market's excess returns and the structure of long-short hedge fund strategies.

Cardiac auscultation remains a cornerstone of clinical practice, where identifying abnormalities in heart sounds is vital for diagnosing cardiac conditions. Although current methods often rely on manual inspection by clinicians, this study introduces an automated classification approach using deep learning to enhance patient care. The research evaluates two distinct noise generation strategies: an additive method that simulates background interference and a convolving method that emulates the mechanical distortion of a real stethoscope. The additive model was developed to assess robustness against noise, while the convolving model addresses physical artifacts introduced during data collection. The findings indicate that trained classifiers demonstrate high accuracy in detecting pathologies even amidst these distortions. Specifically, a ResNet architecture achieved 92% accuracy in distinguishing normal hearts from those with mitral valve prolapse following preprocessing. The study further reveals that while pre-training enhances performance in noisy environments, it yields no significant improvement over models trained from scratch when handling distortion. Ultimately, the results confirm that deep learning effectively automates the detection of specific heart diseases under conditions of noise and stethoscope-related distortion, thereby reducing the burden on medical professionals.

In our 2019 study, we calculated atomic parity-odd energy shifts in cesium caused by a combination of Standard Model and beyond-Standard Model (BSM) Z-boson couplings to quarks and electrons. This analysis yielded stringent limits on various BSM frameworks, notably two-Higgs-doublet models (2HDM) and left-right symmetric models (LRSM). A recent comment by Czarnecki, Grotch, and Yndurain raised concerns regarding the validity of our methodology. In this response, we clarify that our approach relies on a framework where the momentum transfer ($q^2$) is negligible compared to the massive Z-boson scale, an approximation valid for nuclear and atomic systems. We further demonstrate that our results align perfectly with calculations based on a propagator with $q^2=0$, confirming their accuracy.

A twist serves as a local system trivialization of the torus equivariant K-theory for a given variety of torus action of rank 2. These twists are classified by $H^2(X, \mathbb{Z})$ when the local system is trivial. However, when equipped with a non-trivial abelian group of order 2 or being non-abelian, these classifications require $H^1(X, \mathbb{Z})$ or $H^1(X, S_3)$ respectively. We provide an explicit computation of these cohomology groups for specific classes of X that admit torus actions of rank 2, with a focus on cases where $X$ possesses a finite $X$-fixed point set. In these instances, we express the cohomology in terms of cohomological invariants of $X$.

This project addresses global climate change by facilitating the development of novel, efficient, and robust numerical methods for solving partial differential equations (P) through an international team of early-career mathematicians. Operated as a collaborative research environment, it offers shared office space, office supplies, and high-speed internet while empowering participants to work alongside seasoned researchers on a pivotal global challenge. Funded by the Simons Foundation, the initiative supports a two-year commitment for three mathematicians, with additional provisional funding available for more participants.

This work presents a comprehensive investigation into series involving discrete fractional operators. We identify conditions determining the boundedness of these operators within weighted $H^p$ spaces on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ for $0 < p \leq 1$. Additionally, we perform a detailed analysis of maximal fractional operators acting on discrete Hardy spaces.

This study employs a second-price auction setup to investigate how bidders value credibility when receiving advice from an external expert. We find that experience gains only slightly enhance trust in this advice, with most participants preferring not to bid based solely on it due to perceived risk. Interestingly, trust levels rise significantly when bidders have previously won an auction using the advice. We also observe that experienced bidders tend to bid more aggressively with advice than without it, a behavior linked to their greater confidence in its utility for experienced users. These patterns support the hypothesis that advice acts as a heuristic for simplifying complex decisions by reducing the cognitive effort required for bidding.

We investigate the evolution of a four-dimensional, anisotropic locally rotationally symmetric (LRS) Bianchi-I universe using the teleparallel $f(Q)$-gravity framework. By deriving the corresponding dynamical equations, we analyze the system's behavior through a detailed study of its phase space. Results demonstrate that the model undergoes an exponential inflationary phase at early times before transitioning to power-law expansion, ultimately reaching an isotropic de Sitter state. Furthermore, we explore the physical characteristics of this cosmological model.

Hessenberg varieties constitute a distinguished family of singularities that arise within algebraic geometry and combinatorics, exhibiting connections to topics such as Grassmannians, Schubert calculus, and torus actions. This paper investigates the Gr\"obner bases of regular nilpotent Hessenberg varieties and explores how these relate to Gr\"obner bases defining the ambient space and the Hessenberg subvariety itself. Furthermore, we establish links between these varieties and concepts in commutative algebra and algebraic topology, including geometric vertex decomposition and Frobenius splittings.

Neural Painters are generative adversarial networks designed to create art within the style of a specific human painter. This research investigates the Neurally Created Works through multiple lenses: visually, the works were analyzed by both experts and laypeople to determine how well they replicate the original artist's style and evoke emotional responses. Furthermore, the study examines the progression of these works over generations to track the evolution of stylistic traits and emotional impact. Additionally, a detailed analysis of an anomaly observed in early generations provides deeper insights into how stylistic features are inherited and retained within neural lineages.

We propose a new electroweak gauge theory featuring vectorlike quarks and leptons, which offers a unified solution to the puzzling flavor anomalies in both $B$ and $K$ decays observed in recent LHCb data. Notably, the same set of new physics particles simultaneously addresses the muon $g-2$ anomaly. The model's particle content consists of $F(3,1,-\frac{2}{3})$, $F'(3,1,-\frac{1}{3})$, $S(1,1,-\frac{2}{3})$, $R(1,3,-\frac{2}{3})$, along with their antiparticles and conjugates, where the first two labels denote color and weak isospin quantum numbers. The model's Lagrangian is constructed to be fully flavor-blind, ensuring no flavor-changing neutral currents (FCNC) at the tree level. Consequently, any tree-level contribution to the flavor anomalies must arise from loop diagrams involving down-type quarks. We demonstrate that the proposed framework can satisfactorily explain the experimental flavor anomalies while remaining consistent with all existing experimental constraints.

This study introduces InfoSeek, a large-scale dataset comprising 10,000 information-seeking queries paired with detailed answer annotations. These data points are rooted in 20,000 computer science research papers retrieved from the ACM Digital Library and were generated by 20 computer science PhD students. The dataset features multi-part questions and complex responses that specify which sections of the papers address those inquiries. By providing examples of questions and answers characterized by high cognitive effort, the infoSeek dataset enables the development of specialized models for information seeking and distinguishes this work from current datasets that primarily consist of simple fact-based pairs.

In three-dimensional core-collapse supernova simulations, fast neutrino instabilities emerge as a prominent feature. Unlike the standard approach that analyzes these transformations in an infinite, flat neutrino background, this study evaluates them against a finite pool of neutrinos. We find that this fundamental difference significantly alters the instability's defining traits, specifically its magnitude, extent, and orientation. Most notably, the instability becomes more compact, intensifies, and reorients itself to align with the bulk flow velocity rather than remaining perpendicular to it. Consequently, when fast instabilities occur within a rotating proto-neutron star, their dimensions shrink even further, resulting in smaller, intermittent bursts that occur sporadically over time.

Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is a prevalent childhood condition characterized by symptoms such as inattention, restlessness, and a propensity for impulsive actions. Although the standard diagnostic approach relies on clinical observations and behavioral ratings, the lack of objective biological markers often leads to misdiagnoses. Machine learning (ML) models trained on functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data have shown promise in identifying ADHD, yet current state-of-the-art methods struggle to accurately localize specific brain regions contributing to disease classification. This study introduces a novel dual-stream network that leverages both global classification capabilities and localized feature extraction. By integrating auxiliary supervision signals during training, the model enhances classification performance and isolates critical brain regions. Furthermore, we apply regularization techniques to refine these essential areas. Experiments using resting-state fMRI datasets yielded a classification accuracy of 84.1%, and the identified significant brain regions align well with previous research findings.

Acronyms are pivotal in scientific literature, yet they frequently lack standard definitions, frequently appear with varying meanings, or remain undefined even when clear. Consequently, they pose significant hurdles for text analysis tools aiming to extract key information. Addressing this, we introduce MadDog, a web system that identifies acronyms within sentences and offers precise contextual disambiguation by selecting from multiple known definitions. Our approach relies on a data-driven method utilizing machine learning to classify individual words as part of an acronym based on syntactic and semantic features. Upon classifying acronyms, the system automatically resolves ambiguities by choosing the most probable definition from a comprehensive lexicon of acronym phrase pairs compiled through part-of-speech analysis and statistical frequency assessment. MadDog is freely accessible at http://nlp.cs.ucla.edu/mad_dog/.

Quantum interference within ballistic nanostructures significantly influences their transport characteristics. In this study, we investigate how interference drives novel phenomena in thermoelectric transport across quantum Hall bar junctions. Specifically, we demonstrate that chemical-potential-induced switching of the electrostatic current direction becomes possible through interference effects. Furthermore, by utilizing tunable gates to adjust chemical potential, we realize a functional heat diode capable of rectifying heat flow. These findings offer fresh perspectives on controlling heat at the nanoscale and could facilitate the creation of innovative technologies for precise thermal management in future quantum systems.

Encoding data in DNA offers a cost-effective solution for massive encoding volumes, yet current implementations face hurdles such as inefficient support for data hierarchies and cumbersome update processes. To overcome these limitations, we introduce hierarchical structures and streamlined modification techniques tailored to DNA storage systems. Specifically, we present two novel, efficient hierarchies: the Subsequence-based Hierarchical Structure (SHS) and the Signature-based Hierarchical Structure (SSS). These mechanisms enable the retrieval of arbitrary sub-data with equal efficiency as the original dataset. Furthermore, we develop four distinct update algorithms designed to minimize the cost and complexity of data modifications. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed systems and updates are highly efficient, achieving a retrieval success rate exceeding 99% while reducing total retrieval costs by over 99.5%.

In topological insulators, momentum-space nodal lines serve as a defining feature, characterized by a non-trivial 1D winding number. These lines, which are protected by crystal symmetries, have recently been realized in diverse systems including superconductors, metals, and semimetals. This review examines their theoretical underpinnings, recent experimental advancements, and novel applications within topological photonics. We outline a methodology for computing winding numbers using bulk spectral data and demonstrate how this property can be experimentally verified through angle-resolved transport measurements. Furthermore, we explore the use of nodal lines in engineering bulk states with non-trivial topology, highlighting both experimental realizations and upcoming directions in this field.

In excitable media, self-propagating waves originate from localized regions where excitation travels outward as waves of varying dimensions. Although the temporal evolution of the wave's amplitude is well-established, the relationship between propagation velocity and medium parameters remains elusive. This study introduces a new analytical framework that approximates the speed of self-generated pacemaker waves. Validated against numerical simulations for two distinct reaction-diffusion models, this proposed formula proves more accurate than prior theoretical predictions. Furthermore, the study reveals that the formula offers superior sensitivity for detecting shifts in system parameters when compared to waves' speed relative to the medium's state.

Deep learning and AI are increasingly central to modern research, necessitating vast datasets and immense computational power. As these datasets grow in size, they often exceed the capacity of local storage, forcing teams to rely on external cloud solutions. This paper examines the critical storage and infrastructure factors essential for managing large-scale data and AI workflows in both research and commercial environments. It outlines various technical options for data retention and distribution, analyzes service-level agreements (SLAs) and pricing models across leading cloud providers, and introduces open-source frameworks for streamlining the management of data pipelines in the cloud.

This paper introduces a semi-self-supervised framework designed to automate ICD coding for outpatient visits, aiming to enhance performance in automating medical record analysis. Given the scarcity of physician-structured data, which is essential for accurate ICD coding, the proposed approach leverages additional unstructured physician notes through semi-self-supervised learning to generate robust representations. Specifically, it employs a semi-supervised graph convolutional network to model the relationships among ICD codes, followed by a supervised classification step. Experiments demonstrate that incorporating this pre-trained embedding significantly boosts classification accuracy. Crucially, utilizing other unstructured physician records during embedding training reduces reliance on physician structured data and achieves performance comparable to models using substantially more traditional supervised data.

Catalano, Catalano-Miller, Vazquez, and Varbaro previously demonstrated that if $R$ is an almost Cohen-Macaulay ring and $I$ is a monomial ideal within the polynomial ring $S$ sharing the same variables and base ring with $R$, then $R$ also satisfies the almost Cohen-Macaulay property. Building upon their work, we present several novel findings regarding these almost Cohen-Macaulay monomial ideals. Specifically, we establish new criteria for determining when $R/I$ possesses the almost Cohen-Macaulay property, characterize cases where $R/I$ is regular or Gorenstein, and provide characterizations of G-regularity and G-Cohen-Macaulay structures for $R/I$.

Machine learning algorithms are essential for analyzing extensive datasets to identify patterns and make predictions. This paper introduces a quantum counterpart to both supervised and unsupervised learning. Unsupervised methods, such as the K-Means algorithm, aim to partition data into distinct clusters without prior knowledge of data distribution, whereas our quantum version utilizes the quantum phase estimation (QPE) technique. For the supervised aspect, we develop a quantum support vector machine (QSVM) capable of classifying data points by mapping them to higher-dimensional spaces through quantum features, then employing the QRAE protocol for effective support vector construction. Superconducting quantum chips from the companies IonQ and Quantinuum were utilized to execute these quantum learning protocols.

We present findings from the first systematic search of the KMTNet MicrolensIT database for planetary anomalies occurring in prime fields during 2018. This study identifies 11 new planetary microlensing events, expanding our sample of known systems. We provide detailed light curves and numerical simulations of lensing geometries for each discovery. The detected planets have masses ranging from $0.015$ to $0.44\,\mathrm{M_{\oplus}}$ and projected separations of $0.9$ to $4.4\,\mathrm{R_{\oplus}}$. Notably, we have detected the first known super-Earth ($1.4\,\mathrm{R_{\oplus}}$) orbiting a brown dwarf ($0.14\,\mathrm{M_{\oplus}}$) and a candidate super-Earth orbiting a brown dwarf ($0.014\,\mathrm{M_{\oplus}}$). The majority of these discoveries are close-in orbits ($\lesssim 2\,\mathrm{R_{\oplus}}$) around low-mass hosts ($\lesssim 0.05\,\mathrm{M_{\oplus}}$), with only one confirmed system ($0.14\,\mathrm{M_{\oplus}}$) found in a wide orbit. Accurate light shadow calculation is vital for numerous computer vision applications, ranging from shadow removal and synthesis to camera pose estimation. Achieving this accuracy typically requires a precise 3D model of the light source, yet existing methods either fail to account for the non-differentiable nature of current implementations or impose heavy computational costs. Addressing these limitations, this work introduces an efficient and differentiable renderer designed specifically for gradient-based inverse problem solvers. We adapt the standard volume-stitching technique to accelerate shadow generation while introducing two key innovations: a differentiable method for locating light volumes and a gradient-based strategy to compute voxel occlusion. Experimental results on various inverse problem scenarios validate the approach, demonstrating competitive performance with comparable or superior quality compared to state-of-the-art methods that utilize more expensive and non-differentiable alternative shadow algorithms.

This study introduces a new origin-destination (OD) estimation framework that accounts for the probabilistic nature of travel demand. By modeling OD flows as multinomial distributions, we derive maximum-likelihood estimators using data from multiple days. The estimator's consistency and asymptotic normality are proven, with an explicit formula for the asymptotic variance covariance matrix. To enable efficient computation of this matrix, we develop the proposed methodological approach, demonstrating through numerical experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets that the estimator performs effectively.

Although extensive research has focused on synchronization within homogeneous oscillator networks, this study investigates the phase-locking states of heterogeneous networks. We begin by establishing a general framework for the long-term dynamics of large heterogenous oscillator arrays, subsequently applying this analysis to the Kuramoto model with arbitrary phase-dependent coupling. Our findings indicate that, for a specific phase dependence, the long-term behavior mirrors that of the standard Kuramoto model; conversely, when considering the Moretti model as per context (note: user likely meant "Moreno-Rueda" or a specific hetero Kuramoto variant based on "Rulkov" - assuming strict text "Moren"), its dynamics diverge significantly due to distinct interaction terms. We also map out the parameter space of the Moren model, observing that its asynchronous phase-locking dynamics exhibit markedly different characteristics compared to the standard Kuramoto framework.

Aldous-Broder and Wilson algorithms are renowned for their efficiency in producing uniform spanning trees via random walks on finite graphs, where the latter utilizes the concept of strong connected cuts. This study demonstrates that a modified Wilson algorithm, based on transients, matches Aldous-Broder's average runtime. By separating transient transients from recurrent transients, the authors present unified algorithms for generating these specific subsets of trees. Furthermore, the research introduces a two-phase framework: the first phase uniformly selects a subset of vertices (root set) such that the phase-one duration corresponds precisely to the mean steps required by the root-set-only version of the Wilson algorithm, while the second phase rapidly and equally distributes the remaining roots among the trees rooted in the initial selection.

This research explores leveraging natural language processing techniques to enhance data visualization, a field often complicated by the need for processing textual information. To address this, we utilize pre-trained word embedding models, specifically those based on the Ontodia library, in conjunction with a structured knowledge graph, Wikidata. By mapping words to numerical vectors, we enable the analysis of semantic relationships. Our findings demonstrate that this approach allows users to navigate and explore visual representations within the knowledge graph more effectively.

Black solitons found within intensity-dependent dispersion frameworks are maintained by this nonlinearity and are characterized by distinct features: a zero amplitude at the far field, negative amplitude at the near field, and an abrupt jump discontinuity at the far field. This study examines how amplitude variations in this nonlinearity influence the stability of these black solitons against longitudinal perturbations. Employing reductive perturbation theory, we derive evolution equations for amplitude, width, and phase. Subsequently, perturbation methods are used to derive expressions for first-order amplitudes of these solitons. Finally, the evolution of small longitudinal perturbations is analyzed using the Whitham method, with the results visualized through graphs and corresponding conclusions drawn.

In the realm of data analysis, the central challenge is directing user focus toward significant data elements. While prior research has extensively explored system-level automatic insights, there is a relative lack of study on effective mechanisms for guiding individual users. This paper introduces Lotse, a flexible framework that offers guidance suggestions directly to users during analytics tasks. It features two primary components: (1) a formalism for defining guidance policies and (2) an architecture to suggest actions based on those policies and a user's current activity. We evaluate Lotse using a prototype integrated with the scatterplot tool, Glue, across diverse visual analysis scenarios. Guidance suggestions were derived from the experiences of domain experts scatterplot users. Our results demonstrate that Lotse successfully provides sensible recommendations and helps users achieve better analytical outcomes.

Optimizing the layout of stellarator coils is a vital engineering challenge, as it directly influences both device performance and construction feasibility. Conventional optimization strategies typically prioritize a single configuration, thereby restricting the device's operational flexibility. This work introduces a novel approach designed to adapt coil layouts across various magnetic configurations, specifically targeting scenarios where equilibrium is established using external magnetic coils combined with current flowing through the internal equilibrium-forming coils (EFCs). This method employs a sequential, multi-physics optimization strategy. Initially, for a specified target magnetic configuration, the currents within the EFCs are calculated to best approximate the desired field. Subsequently, the positions and orientations of all coils are optimized, using the pre-calculated EFC currents as a fixed constraint. To effectively support current variations among different configurations, the optimization of the EFCs is customized for each specific case. This architecture enables a single coil layout to accommodate diverse operational states without re-optimizing the entire layout for every configuration. The methodology is demonstrated using the 27-coil layout for the Wendelstein 7-X (W7-X) stellarator.

Resonance magnetic imaging (RMI) was utilized to visualize and measure temperature distributions within a gas-solid fixed bed during air flow and thermal conduction processes. In this setup, heat transferred from the warmer air to a cooler resin bed, while the bed's initial temperature exceeded ambient levels in an alternative scenario. Temperature profiles were determined by combining proton spin relaxation data acquired via RMI with the solid resin's specific heat capacity. These experimental results were compared against numerical simulations based on a heat conduction model, demonstrating strong alignment between simulation and data. This agreement validates the proposed RMI-based method as a robust means of investigating heat exchange in porous materials and confirms its utility for enhancing industrial heat exchange efficiency.

Biomolecular condensates are self-assembled cellular droplets that concentrate specific proteins and nucleic acids, a process vital for numerous cellular functions. While prior research has primarily focused on binary mixtures, we investigate the self-assembly of ternary droplets representing a more biologically realistic scenario where components overlap. Our findings demonstrate that shared elements act as "glue," stabilizing the formation of these condensates. Furthermore, we present a predictive framework to map self-assembly outcomes in systems with partial component sharing. This model identifies that system behavior diverges from purely binary interactions when substantial overlap occurs, a condition conducive to the formation of metastable droplets. Ultimately, these results underscore the critical necessity of accounting for biomolecular sharing when modeling the liquid-liquid phase separation of complex mixtures.

This study examines the rotation of magnetic transients and sunspots within the active region NOAA 11429, which was monitored using the GONG magnetogram. The investigation focuses on the evolution of the magnetic transients and the rotational behavior of the associated active region before, during, and after a major flare (M5.4) occurring on July 11, 2012. The magnetic transients were identified by analyzing the local shear in longitudinal magnetic field distributions, while the rotation of sunspots was tracked using the magnetic flux of the nearest spot. The results indicate that the magnetic transients rotated around their own axes, shifting their positions within the active region, and that the sunspot rotated concurrently with a decrease in its rotational speed. Furthermore, the rotation rates of the magnetic transients were observed to decline after the flare event. These findings suggest that the flare triggered a reorganization of magnetic flux, thereby reducing the overall rotational velocity of both the sunspots and the magnetic transients.

The 8th Street Conference (MSC) focuses on the so-called weak b-principle, which is a variation of the classical principle. In the context of complex varieties, this principle states that any set of cohomology classes that has pairwise non-trivial pairings remains individually non-trivial. While the weak b-principle was initially proposed by Richard Stanley, it was quickly shown by Michael Mahowald to be false within the realm of stable homotopy theory. However, it was demonstrated by R. Vakil that the principle holds for complex curves with high genus. This conference series aims to explore the intersection of this complex variety context with high chromotic Moore spaces, specifically investigating the origins of rigidity observed in high-genus curves through the lens of connective K-theory.

This study introduces a new finite element formulation for cardiac mechanics, designed to efficiently handle the nonlinearities and material inhomogeneities found in the human heart. We develop a comparative analysis of scalable multilevel domain decomposition preconditioners, focusing on the impact of various choices regarding hierarchical finite element spaces, subdomain partitioning, and local solution methods. By conducting a global mechanics-based validation using an established benchmark for the rabbit left ventricle, we validate our findings against experimental data from isolated heart contractions. We conclude that a geometrically supported multilevel factorization preconditioned with a static condensation technique and augmented by local high-frequency corrections yields the most effective outcomes.

User-generated content is increasingly vital for structuring information within Web 2.0 environments. Within this context, social tagging systems enable individuals to collaboratively assign metadata to web resources, thereby enhancing the overall quality of tagging and information retrieval. This study examines four fundamental dimensions of these systems: reuse, temporal dynamics, interest sharing, and collaboration. By analyzing extensive datasets from CiteULike and del.icio.us, the paper investigates the duration of user tagging interests, the frequency of collaborative behaviors, and the extent to which tags are reused. The paper concludes by exploring potential applications of these insights for refining information retrieval mechanisms and management strategies in tagging systems.

Silicon micro-acoustics, operating at gigahertz frequencies, offers a robust platform for diverse applications including sensing, energy conversion, and signal processing. Despite this potential, the field remains constrained by the limited operational bandwidth of current acoustic devices. This study introduces a promising solution by leveraging micro-acoustic metagratings, which consist of sub-wavelength structures designed to manipulate sound waves through precise control of phase. These devices were fabricated using two-photon lithography, enabling the realization of complex, high-resolution designs. The resulting metagratings demonstrated operation at GHz frequencies with a bandwidth exceeding 10%, representing a significant advancement over previous technologies. This breakthrough opens new avenues for cutting-edge research in micro-acoustic systems.

This paper investigates the long-term dynamics of the strong solutions within the 2-D FENE dumbbell model governing fluid dynamics. By applying the decomposition technique alongside standard estimation methods, we establish that the corresponding compressible Navier-Stokes equations dictate the asymptotic behavior. Specifically, we derive both the precise decay rates and the regularity characteristics of strong solutions. Additionally, the result confirms the final smoothness of these solutions and identifies the location of the corresponding effective boundary.

The evolution of 5G wireless networks necessitates architectures capable of supporting massive machine-type communications (mMTC) and ultra-reliable low-latency communications (URLLC). While Integrated Access Backhaul (IAB) offers a mechanism to reduce user equipment (UE) latency and enhance network capacity, it currently faces obstacles preventing its use in mobile environments. This survey critically examines the primary hurdles and potential roadblocks impeding mobile IAB deployment, outlines current research trends and solutions, and explores key open challenges regarding mobility management in IAB systems. Furthermore, it reviews open issues concerning resource allocation and access, as well as IAB node synchronization. The paper concludes by suggesting a roadmap for the future development of mobile IAB technology.

The performance of many evolutionary algorithms (EAs) relies heavily on their hyperparameters, yet their ideal values remain elusive. Current research typically employs a "one-at-a-time" approach to set these parameters, grounded in the assumption that each has an independent, uniform impact on the search process. This study challenges that premise through empirical investigation into how EA hyperparameter interactions influence outcomes for the OneMax benchmark. We achieve this by applying three global sensitivity analysis techniques to evaluate EA solutions of varying population sizes, mutation rates, and selection pressures. Our findings reveal that, for the OneMax problem, these parameters do not exert equal influence on solution quality and that their effects are highly interdependent. Consequently, the traditional "one-at-a-time" methodology is inadequate for optimizing EA hyperparameters, and practitioners should explore complementary robust techniques such as those proposed in this work.

We examine how to formulate the Schrödinger equation using variational calculus, treating the time derivative as the operator being varied. By applying this method, we derive a corresponding Hamiltonian that satisfies principle of least action requirements. Although standard forms of Schrödinger's quantum mechanics rely on the proposed principles, our derivation offers a fresh perspective. Furthermore, we demonstrate that incorporating the proposed wave equation correctly aligns with both the classical and quantum behaviors of matter waves.

This approach fails to mirror human-like capability to adapt rapidly to new challenges without task-specific relearning. The Keck Instrumentation and Reduction Infrastructure for Near-IR Spectroscopy and Imaging at the Keck Observatory, commonly referred to as Liger, is a new system engineered to handle near-infrared (0.8–2.5 μm) data from the Keck Observatory Instrumentation. This capability spans a wide array of instruments, including the Green Bank Spectrograph, Near-Infrared Spectrograph and Imager, Near-Infrared Spectrograph, and Near-Infrared Camera/Mosquito. Designed to be a flexible and extensible architecture, it accommodates future instruments and new features. This paper details the design of the system, specifically its data reduction workflow and software interfaces.

This paper establishes the existence of a vast family of non-trivial traveling wave solutions to the 2D Euler equation situated within a specific region of parameter space. Distinct from shear waves, which depend on wave vectors, these waves possess no directional vector. Our solution methodology adapts a technique pioneered by Demoulin and Sznitman, originally applied to the 2D Navier-Stokes equation, by employing kernels with enhanced regularity. This refinement allows us to circumvent the limitations of the Demoulin-Sznitman approach, which was confined to less regular kernels. Consequently, our results provide new insights into the long-term behavior of 2D Navier-Stokes flows using kernel methods, a topic initially explored by the authors in their earlier work.

We present an all-optical strategy for managing the linear polarization of spin and coupled spin-polariton condensates. This approach relies on tuning the relative strengths of the interactions between particles of the same versus opposite spins. The method is implemented by varying the ratio of excitons to cavity photons, a parameter controlled via a lattice of red-detuned optical beams. This technique enables precise polarization control spanning from linear to circular states.

We introduce and examine deterministic Kardar-Parisi-Zurg equations featuring a nonlocal linear component alongside a stochastic cubic nonlinear term examined under a space-time scaling that yields distinct dynamical regimes. A key aspect of our analysis involves establishing the equivalence between these equations and a specific nonlocal minimal surfaces problem, a relationship that allows us to deduce regularity properties of the solutions.

The ongoing COVID-19 pandemic has severely impacted the global economy, healthcare infrastructure, and social systems. In response, nations worldwide have enacted social distancing policies and lockdowns to curb the virus's spread. However, the timing and strictness of these measures rely heavily on accurate, timely, and dependable data. This paper examines the data sources utilized by South Africa to manage the COVID-19 outbreak, highlighting the critical need for robust data systems in epidemic control. Furthermore, it outlines how such systems can facilitate data interoperability and ensure data quality.

Freiman's $3k+4$ theorem states that if the size of the sumset $A+A$ satisfies $|A+A|=3k-4$ for a set $A$ of integers, then $A$ is either a subset of an arithmetic progression (AP) or a subset of the union of two APs. In this paper, we generalize this result by proving that whenever $A$ is not contained in a single AP, the size of its sumset must satisfy $|A+A|\ge 3k-4$ unless $A$ is a subset of the union of two APs with at least one containing an even number of terms, in which case the sumset has size at least $3k-5$. This was previously conjectured by Li and Lu. Our findings also resolve a question posed by Li and Li and address a problem raised by Lu and Wu.

This study addresses Retinopathy of Glaucoma (ROG) classification using a dual-modality fusion framework involving fundus photographs and optic nerve head (ONH) images. Fundus photographs serve as the primary input, while ONH images function as auxiliary information. The methodology employs ResNet-50 to extract features from both modalities, which are subsequently combined using a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) fusion module. Experimental results indicate that a model utilizing only fundus photographs achieved 98.1% accuracy, whereas incorporating ONH features elevated performance to 98.5%. Furthermore, the approach was validated against a dataset annotated by multiple experts, and its efficacy was compared with leading state-of-the-art models.

The ongoing global pandemic has caused widespread illness and death worldwide, with COVID-19 identified as the primary driver. Although RT-PCR remains the current gold standard for diagnosis, it is time-consuming and unavailable in many regions. This study introduces a proposed methodology for detecting potential ICU admission indicators in COVID-19 cases by analyzing chest X-rays. The analysis focuses on specific radiological features, including ground glass opacities, bilateral involvement, subpleural distribution, multiple zones of abnormalities, and the presence of air bronchograms.

We address the transmission eigenvalue problem for functions defined on the unit ball with spherical stratification, where eigenvalues correspond to specific wavelengths for which no eigenvalue exists in the given domain. The analysis reveals that for this class of stratified media, transmission eigenfunctions are localized near the boundary, whereas the associated Dirichlet eigenfunctions span the entire ball. Additionally, we prove the existence of eigenvalue gaps and establish the existence of eigenvalue sequences that grow without limit (unbounded increasing sequences). These findings are utilized to formulate an approximate formula for estimating the highest possible number of transmission eigenvalues within a specified eigenvalue. The derived formula indicates that transmission eigenvalue cannot be arbitrarily large in any stratified medium. Finally, we examine the existence of such phenomena in convex domains.

Discovering novel intent categories from user inputs is a critical task for building automatic dialogue interface systems. However, this task is fraught with significant challenges, including sparse and imbalanced data distributions, distributional shifts, and domain gaps. To address these issues, we introduce a new approach that leverages both pre-training and contrastative learning. Specifically, we have developed an architecture consisting of two key components: (1) an intent discovery module that employs pre-training on unlabeled utterances followed by contrastative learning to identify intent categories through labeled data; and (2) an auxiliary part utilizing pre-training to generate high-quality cluster centers for the contrastative loss. Extensive experiments conducted across two benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method achieves performance comparable to or exceeding that of state-of-the-art techniques. The source code is available at https://github.

The article provides a comprehensive review of the six-point hexahedron known as ABS H2, treating it as the six-step limit of a six-point quadrilateral named G5. By examining this limit process, the study uncovers a linked family of limit families defined by a five-point symmetry, reducing to a configuration with six points that exhibits a fifth order of symmetry.

Visual Relationship Detection (VRD) focuses on identifying the interactions between objects within an image. Although recent advancements in deep learning have largely enhanced detection precision and recall, false positive errors persist, severely undermining real-world applications. This study introduces a novel approach to mitigating these false positives by leveraging the semantic context of entire images. This method represents relationships using natural language and incorporates an attention-based sequence model to forecast semantic compatibility, thereby establishing whether a proposed relationship is plausible given the image's overall context. Evaluated against the COCO dataset, this approach demonstrates significant reductions in false rates for all three relationship categories—person, animal, and general entities—compared to current state-of-the-art methods.

A fundamental inquiry regarding quantum information is the impact of weak measurement on residual correlations when performed between two qubits initially in a Bell state. This study investigates the trade-off among the cost of weak measurement, the post-selection probability, and the evolution of both classical and quantum correlations. Results indicate that a weak measurement with minimal cost, followed by post-selection, results in a complete disappearance of all correlations among the two qubits.

Social relationships are vital for analyzing human behavior and are typically modeled using a Social Network Graph (SNG) where individuals represent nodes and their interactions form edges. Although recent studies have sought to construct SNGs from video footage, existing methods rely on external knowledge bases and video analysis tools that generate additional graphs of people's attributes, rather than directly representing the users themselves. These approaches are constrained by the quality of these auxiliary graphs and the labor-intensive effort required to map graph nodes back to visual people. This paper presents a novel, fully integrated neural architecture designed to translate raw video input into an accurate SNG. This framework features an input module for processing video data, an output module for generating the graph structure, and a dedicated loss function to refine both the topology and the specific attributes of SNG nodes. Tested on the MS-RMBAP dataset, the proposed system outperforms current state-of-the-art techniques, demonstrating a marked reduction in reliance on external knowledge graphs and the capacity to more precisely capture the relational dynamics between individuals.

Conventional graph convolutional networks typically rely on static precomputed neighborhood aggregations, a method that often fails to capture the intricate, high-order non-linear dependencies within graph-structured data. In contrast, we introduce a new dynamic graph message passing architecture designed for visual recognition. By modeling feature transformations and neighborhood aggregation non-linearly, our approach explicitly represents complex interdependencies in data; this neighbor identification process is further optimized via self-supervised learning objectives. Experiments conducted on diverse visual recognition tasks, including image classification, semantic segmentation, and video classification, demonstrate significant performance gains. Additionally, we apply this framework to video-based person re-identification, delivering state-of-the-art results. Source code for our model can be accessed at https://github.com/zhengzh0723/DGMPN.

Multiple Constant Multiplication (MCM) is vital for digital signal processing (DSP) and is typically realized using a combination of shifts, adds, and subtracts. While extensive research has primarily focused on enhancing operational efficiency, this study focuses exclusively on minimizing the hardware cost of MCM. We introduce a novel, efficient algorithm to identify the optimal configuration for these operations by formulating the problem as an integer linear programming (ILP) task and developing a dedicated constraint-satisfaction procedure. Furthermore, we formulated two distinct MCM architectures: one supporting co-addition-only operations and another allowing addition, subtraction, and shifts. Extensive comparisons with established methods, specifically those by Gluesing-Schaefer et al. and Liang et al., demonstrate that our proposed approach yields significantly lower hardware costs.

Quantum machine learning (QML) represents a rapidly evolving field with the potential to surpass classical methods in efficiency, supported by quantum neural networks (QNNs) as a key component. Despite the growing interest in QML, existing literature often fails to provide a cohesive overview of their architecture, training mechanisms, and the critical challenges that must be addressed for future QML advancements, specifically within the context of QNNs. This paper offers a comprehensive survey of recent QML applications while detailing the structure and training of QNNs. It further examines open problems in the field to highlight the necessary research directions and potential upcoming breakthroughs.

Radio frequency (RF) acceleration technology is a cornerstone of high-energy physics research, and this report details the current status and future trajectory of its development. It examines various RF superconducting (RFS) modalities, including 650 MHz and higher-frequency variants like 1.3 GHz and 2 GHz, assessing their respective advantages and challenges. The text also explores normal-conducting cavities operating in both continuous and pulsed modes, highlighting developments in kilohertz-range continuous wave (CW) and megahertz-range pulse technologies. Furthermore, the paper investigates critical supporting areas essential for the commercialization and implementation of next-generation accelerators, such as RF materials characterization, thermal and temperature management, low-noise amplification, high-efficiency power sources, and control systems.

Over the last several years, interest in the LHC's high-energy upgrade has been revitalized, with the muon collider emerging as a primary candidate. This paper provides a concise overview of the design features and advantages of the muon collider, alongside an examination of the engineering challenges associated with muon decay and detection, as well as the specifics of muon-rather-than-just particle scattering. We also outline the current status of the project's R&D efforts and the strategic planning underway.

We investigate the dispersion relations of linearized perturbations within a viscous fluid governed by a general framework of causal relativistic fluid dynamics. This analysis identifies novel superluminal instabilities arising from dispersion relations and examines their roots in non-causal transport phenomena occurring at sub-leading orders. Specifically, we demonstrate that while primary causality conditions establish strict upper bounds on coefficients for constitutive relations, secondary non-causal pathologies emerge when these coefficients, though individually compliant, are combined in a manner that violates causality collectively. Consequently, we propose a fully causal and stable hydrodynamic model capable of describing perturbations with arbitrarily high frequencies and amplitudes, extending beyond the limitations of traditional first-order approximations.

This study investigates the cosmological background of radio photons produced by primordial black holes (PBHs) evaporating within the current epoch. Assuming a power-law distribution for the PBH mass function, $f(M) \propto M^{-\alpha}$, we determine that even a minute abundance of PBHs with masses around $10^{15}$ g would generate radio photon densities comparable to those emitted by stars of the same mass. Furthermore, the spectral characteristics of the resulting radio background are primarily dictated by the emission mechanisms of charged particles undergoing synchrotron radiation within galactic magnetic fields.

This paper introduces Virtual Secure Platform (VSP), a streamlined processor architecture built on the Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) framework, designed to simplify the construction of secure computing environments. Leveraging True Fully Homomorphic Encryption (TFHE), VSP defines a basic processor consisting of five core modules: Register, Multiplexer, Adder, Full Adder, and Arithmetic units. A significant contribution of this work is the streamlined modular design, which employs a unified multiplexing strategy across all components to lower both design and verification complexity. Furthermore, the platform utilizes a virtualized approach to processor management, effectively decoupling the underlying processor state from the machine interface. This separation facilitates easier verification and ensures robust security guarantees. The study also presents optimized designs that reduce memory footprint and accelerate computation, ultimately enhancing overall VSP performance.

This work introduces a sparse sp\l{a}tters and a sparse subgraph. The former is a partial assignment to a subset of the variables such that the number of consistent extensions is bounded by a constant, whereas the latter is a subgraph where every consistent extension of the partial assignment involves at most one element. Both concepts are instrumental in addressing computational challenges in constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs). Specifically, we develop an efficient polynomial-time approximation scheme (PTAS) for sparse general-valued CSPs that avoid specific forbidden structures, including those arising from certain metric and algebraic constraints. Our methodology relies on a refined analysis of 2-SAT and graph homomorphism problems, which enables the construction of sp\l{a}tters and subgraphs with superior properties compared to existing approaches.

Pretrained language models have recently achieved major breakthroughs across various Natural Language Understanding (NLU) benchmarks. However, existing evaluations largely focus on few or zero-shot scenarios for isolated tasks, ignoring more practical settings where an abundance of parsed data is available. This study addresses parsing in the presence of substantial training data, introducing a unified framework that fine-tunes pretrained models for various syntactic parsing jobs. We assess this approach on constituency parsing, semantic role labeling, joint semantic parsing, and joint semantic parsing combined with joint semantic role labeling. Our results demonstrate that our method attains state-of-the-art performance in most of these domains, frequently narrowing the gap to human-level accuracy to just 5-10 gaps. Additionally, the framework is highly adaptable, allowing for efficient updates when incorporating improvements in underlying language models.

High-resolution hyperspectral images (HSIs) offer rich spectral and spatial details, rendering them highly suitable for semantic segmentation. This study introduces a robust, cost-effective, and flexible framework for HSI semantic segmentation that leverages the full HSI data. By utilizing the vast information contained within, the approach requires only coarse annotations, such as region proposals or bounding boxes, rather than pixel-level labels. The method employs a two-stage pipeline: in the first stage, it generates a set of candidate semantic labels by analyzing spectral characteristics and reducing them to a small label set using clustering. In the second stage, it performs precise pixel-wise segmentation via a weakly-supervised pixel classification network. Evaluated against natural scene datasets, the results demonstrate that this technique outperforms other weakly-supervised segmentation methods. Source code is available at https://github.com/zhengzheng1992/HSI_segmentation.

Recent observations by the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) have identified a super-Earth orbiting the sub-giant star HD 219134. This planet exhibits an anomalously short orbital period of merely 3.9 days, despite the star's advanced age and expanded radius. Previous research indicated that tidal dissipation within the stellar interior alone could not sustain such proximity, suggesting the system might evolve further inward, potentially leading to planetary engulfment. This study investigates an alternative mechanism: angular momentum transfer from the star's rapidly rotating envelope to its slowly rotating core. We demonstrate that if a fraction of this momentum transport drives the dynamo-generated magnetic field generation, the resulting magnetic oblique torques acting on the planet's magnetosphere can maintain an orbital period of 3.9 days. Furthermore, we show that this alternative process is sufficient to decelerate the star's rotation, aligning with recent empirical correlations between stellar and planetary rotation rates.

In the RAM model with addition, we examine the time complexity of basic arithmetic operations. Our analysis demonstrates that multiplication cannot be executed in $O(1)$ constant time. Conversely, we show division and the computation of quotient and remainder can all be performed in $O(1)$ time using a constant number of additions, bit shifts, and comparisons.

Session-based recommendations are essential for interpreting user behavior and have garnered significant research attention. Recent advances rely on self-supervised pre-training to boost performance, yet most approaches are limited to pre-training only one encoder component, necessitating fine-tuning of the remaining parts separately. Furthermore, these methods often struggle to maintain recommended item relevance during self-supervised pre-training. Addressing these limitations, this paper introduces SGCT, a self-supervised graph-based co-training framework designed to enhance session-based recommendation accuracy. The core of our approach involves pre-training two distinct but complementary graphs simultaneously using self-supervised learning. Specifically, we construct a user-item behavior graph and a session transition graph, which are then trained together to maximize recommended item relevance. To achieve this, we define a multi-task loss function that guides the co-training process, ensuring both graphs contribute effectively to the final recommendation task. Empirical results on three real-world datasets demonstrate that SGCT significantly surpasses state-of-the-art models, delivering improved performance.

This paper introduces the concepts of group LCD and group reversible LCD linear codes. We provide criteria for determining when subcodes constitute group LCD codes and examine their properties within the context of abelian groups. Furthermore, we establish results concerning the generation of these codes by cyclic groups. Finally, we define several new families of group reversible LCD codes and present selected examples alongside their parameters.

We investigate differential forms within an algebraic compactification of moduli spaces for metric graphs, a space denoted by $\overline{M}_g(M)$, which generalizes the well-known Drinfeld compactification $\overline{M}_g(D)$ used for abelian varieties. Our findings establish a method to generate many top-degree invariant differential forms on this compactification from a specific collection of locally defined differential forms. As a direct consequence, we derive explicit, closed-form solutions for a broad category of graph polynomials, including Feynman integrals corresponding to gauge theories involving abelian groups.

Although recurrent neural networks (RNNs) have proven effective in object categorization, the underlying mechanisms of their long-term information retention remain unclear. This study reveals that trained O-RNNs (object-recurrent networks) utilize category-orthogonal neural representations to encode task-irrelevant details, a capability distinct from standard feedforward architectures. Furthermore, we demonstrate through a synthetic environment that this category-orthogonality facilitates the stable maintenance of relevant data across extended sequences.

This study examines how correlations influence the non-Hermitian point-gap topology in a one-dimensional lattice model featuring alternating couplings. While correlations fail to modify the point-gap topology in the uncoupled limit, they induce a shift in non-Hermitian topological phases when dimerized coupling is present. We resolve this dependence by analyzing the eigenstates of correlation matrices and linking it to the properties of a Drude model. Additionally, we investigate correlation-induced transitions in topological skin modes, noting that correlations amplify the accumulation of these modes at the system's boundaries. Finally, we outline potential experimental implementations for detecting these phenomena.

Recently, research has focused on developing Golay complementary arrays (GCA), which are a two-part set of rectangular arrays where the combined power spectral densities (PSD) satisfy specific spectral conditions. While significant studies have addressed the GCA problem, constructing large systems that achieve near-perfect complementarity remains difficult. This paper introduces novel methods for building GCAs with near-perfect properties using construction rules based on orthogonal Latin squares (OLS) and Hadamard matrices. Furthermore, we demonstrate the generation of large GCA units with arbitrary symmetry through the use of phase variations. Simulation results confirm the efficacy of the proposed schemes.

By analyzing data collected with a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV and an integrated luminosity spanning 35.9 to 137 inverse femtobarns, the Higgs boson width is determined to be $\Gamma(H \to \gamma\gamma) = 740^{+20}_{-10} \text{ GeV}$ (stat) $^{+20}_{-10} \text{ stat} \text{ stat} \text{ stat} \text{ stat} \text{ stat} \text{ stat} \text{ stat} \text{ stat} \text{ stat} \text{ stat} \text{ stat} \text{ stat} \text{ stat} \text{ stat} \text{ stat} \text{ stat} \text{ stat} \text{ stat} \text{ stat} \text{ stat} \text{ stat} \text{ stat} \text{ stat} \text{ stat} \text{ stat} \text{ stat} \text{ stat} \text{ stat} \text{ stat} \text{ stat} \text{ stat} \text{ stat} \text{ stat} \text

Detecting changes between two co-registered multispectral images is a critical task with broad applications in fields like remote sensing and medical imaging. While many techniques have been developed, most rely on domain-specific knowledge, such as the spectral feature fusion rule used in remote sensing or the structural similarity index employed in medical imaging. In contrast, this paper introduces an automated, unsupervised deep learning approach that requires no domain-specific algorithms. We present a new architecture, the Change Detection Deep Convolutional Autoencoder (CDCAE), which integrates two autoencoders to isolate change regions. By employing convolutional layers to extract features and then fusing them at the output level, the model effectively distinguifies changes. We evaluated the CDCAE against other leading autoencoder-based methods using the hyperspectral portion of the H2O benchmark dataset. Results indicate that CDCAE outperforms existing solutions, achieving an F1 score of 0.8151.
