In finite element simulations involving fluid flow, accuracy is often limited by discretisation errors on the vector transport equation. This study introduces a simplified, fully explicit temporal scheme for discretising that equation on non-structured tetrahedral and hexahedral meshes. By integrating a newly derived analytical formula with a streamlined time-integration strategy, the method achieves a significant reduction in computational cost. When applied specifically to quadrilateral finite elements of the lowest-order Raviart-Thomas type, the approach yields a spatially fully implicit algorithm. A four-stage Runge-Kutta scheme is employed to overcome the inherent implicit constraints, enabling fully explicit solutions. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed method delivers both high precision and computational efficiency.

Federated learning (FL) has emerged as a robust privacy framework for machine learning, enabling decentralized training while ensuring data never leaves the client devices. Recently, researchers have investigated how to integrate fairness and differential privacy (DP) within FL systems. This paper re-examines differential privacy bounds in FL, introducing a practical method for measuring and achieving privacy during model aggregation. It demonstrates that widely adopted heterogeneous DP implementations often result in looser privacy guarantees than theoretically expected, prompting the proposal of a refined, clients-centric privacy aggregation protocol. Concurrently, we address the challenge of ensuring demographic fairness across both central DP and specific non-central fairness-enhancing techniques. We introduce an adaptive approach that dynamically adjusts learning rates to mitigate biases inherent in dominant clients, effectively equalizing their influence. Empirical evaluations on standard image classification benchmarks indicate that our aggregation strategies significantly improve differential privacy bounds with negligible impact on accuracy. Moreover, the proposed fairness algorithms successfully reduce demographic disparities more effectively than existing solutions.

The LHCb collaboration reports evidence for an excited $B_c^+$ state, denoted as $\bar{b}c1$, observed via its decay into $J/\psi \bar{K}^0$. Statistical significance reaches $9.2\sigma$, with measured mass and width values of $6.879 \pm 0.012 \text{ (stat)} \pm 0.010 \text{ (syst)} \text{ GeV}/c^2$ and $0.62 \pm 0.18 \text{ (stat)} \pm 0.10 \text{ (syst)} \text{ MeV}/c^2$, respectively. The observed spectral structure is consistent with a $\bar{b}c1(2P)$ assignment, though a $\bar{b}c1(2S)$ hypothesis remains possible.

Recent advances in efficiently solving Hamiltonian numerics led to introducing a continuous Runge-Kutta method with $s$ stages that approximates problem (1). When applied to a test ODE, this method generates $s$ intermediate trajectories connecting two time points. We demonstrate that these intermediate paths form an $s$-stage quadrature rule with maximal possible order order $2s$. Specifically, this method exactly integrates all polynomials up to degree $s$ exactly along each of the $s$ stages. Applying this to a specific ordinary differential equation yields a Runge-Kutta method of order $2s$ with special structure. We call this a "continuous Runge-Kutta method of order $2s$."

Model-parallel deep learning has emerged as a viable approach for training extremely large neural networks, enabling systems to exceed the memory limits of individual GPUs by distributing network layers across multiple devices. This method, however, introduces significant communication overhead that diminishes its efficiency compared to alternative parallelization strategies. To mitigate this communication burden, we propose a local critic training framework designed to further cut connections between devices. By leveraging each local network's partial view of the global data distribution, the approach trains localized critics to produce better parameter initial estimates, thereby narrowing the communication window for synchronization. We demonstrate the method's efficacy through an eight-device implementation of ResNet-152, showing a 40% reduction in total communication costs while maintaining parity in convergence speed and solution quality.

Three-dimensional chaotic scattering systems featuring Wada fractals—where basins sharing a common boundary form a connected set—were investigated. Our findings reveal that these Wada basins are typically three-way configurations separated by mutually intricate boundaries. Specifically, in the unscaled system, the boundaries consist of two overlapping chaotic layers, whereas introducing mild dissipation causes these layers to merge into a single layer accompanied by a novel, previously unseen Wada boundary structure. This new topology arises from the intersection of two distinct chaotic layers, each draped over a separate primary chaotic saddle, with the resulting fractal geometry dictated by the system's parameters. Furthermore, we derived criteria to anticipate both the emergence of these Wada boundaries and the overall basin-mapping topology, noting that slight variations in parameters can trigger a basins' reorganization. Most significantly, our results demonstrate that low levels of dissipation can actually expand the attraction domains of certain basins, indicating that the optimal level of energy loss for maximizing basin sizes is not invariably minimal.

We investigate a scenario where the bottom quark transitions into up quarks mediated by a light boson, $B$, which exists in the sub-GeV to multi-GeV mass range. In this framework, $B$ mediates the decay of muons into neutron-proton pairs, $\mu^- N 	o 
u_\mu n p$. Although this process is suppressed by the smallness of the neutron-proton cross section, it stands out as the leading channel for detecting long-lived particles in experiments like SHiP and LHCb. Our analysis demonstrates that for boson lifetimes exceeding approximately 10 meters, the total event yield in SHiSh is roughly an order of magnitude higher from $\mu^- N 	o 
u_\mu n n \alpha$ compared to the flavor-conserving channel $\mu^- N 	o e^- N 
u_e 
u_\mu$. Consequently, this flavor-changing process becomes crucial for probing long-lived light particles, specifically when the lifetime surpasses 10 meters.

Recognizing human actions within videos is a fundamental and demanding computer vision challenge. Although recent deep learning approaches have yielded notable progress, their heavy computational demands and susceptibility to overfitting on small datasets remain significant hurdles. This study introduces a Hierarchical Attention Network (HAN) designed to enhance efficient and precise action recognition. The proposed architecture employs two attention mechanisms: the first aggregates spatial information from individual video frames, while the second distills temporal information across the sequence of feature maps. Unlike standard action recognition pipelines that utilize frame-level attention followed by global average pooling, our second attention layer is parameterized and explicitly focuses on the most discriminative features identified by the first mechanism. This hierarchical attention structure not only curtails computational load but also mitigates negative side effects stemming from uninformative data. Experimental results on the UCF101 and HMDB51 benchmarks demonstrate that the HAN achieves superior accuracy compared to existing methods while maintaining significantly lower training and inference costs.

The weak cosmic censorship conjecture (WCCC) remains a significant focus within general rel theory, with recent efforts dedicated to verifying its validity in various settings. In this study, we investigate the scalar field's impact on the thermodynamics and WCCC of the Reissner-Nordström anti - de Sitter (RNS dS) black hole. Our findings demonstrate that scalar field perturbations can trigger the disappearance of the event horizon, thereby confirming the WCCC. Furthermore, our thermodynamic analysis indicates that while specific heat diverges near the extremal limit, no Hawking-Page phase transition occurs under these conditions.

This piece offers a brief overview of the principles surrounding star formation, the life cycle of stars, and stellar remnants.
Stellar formation occurs within the dense regions of molecular clouds, where gravity causes dust and gas to contract.
This contraction continues until nuclear fusion ignites in the core, marking the emergence of a new star.
Once formed, a star remains stable for the majority of its existence as fusion counteracts gravitational collapse.
However, eventually, fusion ceases, and gravity overwhelms the outward pressure, causing the star to expand into a red giant.
The subsequent evolution depends entirely on the star's mass:
Low-mass stars shed their outer layers to form planetary nebulae, leaving behind white dwarf remnants that gradually cool over eons.
High-mass stars undergo catastrophic supernova explosions, yielding neutron stars or black holes as their cores collapse.
These dense remnants persist for billions of years before ultimately disappearing through Hawking radiation.
*Note: This overview is intended primarily for educational purposes.*

The concept of entropy is central to physics, and the primary objective of this work is to calculate the entropies of various spin models. To achieve this, we employ the Nested Sampling algorithm, a technique originally devised for inferring the posterior distribution of parameters in Bayesian model analysis. Within this framework, the entropy is determined by differentiating the Bayesian evidence with regard to the evidence parameter. We demonstrate the application of this method to both the one-dimensional and two-dimensional Ising models, as well as the XY model.

We present a novel concept termed "tempered test functions" and utilize it to define novel classes of measure-valved solutions for nonlinear hyperbolic conservation laws. The established result demonstrates the equivalence between these proposed temperered measures and standard Radon measures; however, it is worth noting that while this equivalence holds, the new frameworks provide significant benefits by permitting test functions that are more singular than traditional classes allow.

Network attacks are evolving continuously, necessitating the development of ever more sophisticated detection mechanisms. While machine learning offers a robust solution, it is often hindered by the resource constraints of devices, where limited storage and processing capabilities prevent the deployment of complex algorithms. To address this, we introduce NB coded, a two-stage attack classification system designed specifically for resource-constrained environments. The method first employs a dimensionality reduction technique using Discrete Cosine Transformation (DCT) to compress feature vectors, followed by a classifer based on the Naive Bayes model trained on the reduced dataset. We evaluated NB coded against various combinations of dimensionality reduction algorithms and classifier alternatives. Results demonstrate that the proposed classification pipeline outperforms existing solutions in terms of accuracy while maintaining lower computational demands for both processing time and memory usage.

This paper examines the Schreier growth series of all finitely generated abelian-by-finitely solvable groups that admit a polycyclic structure, alongside the Schreier growth series of finitely generated solvable groups equipped with a rational series. Additionally, we present multiple examples demonstrating the existence of finitely presented solvable groups exhibiting exponential but non-computable growth.

Understanding the dynamics of biological movement is a key area of biomechanics, a field that relies on video-based motion tracking to record and analyze an organism's trajectory, angles, and accelerations. This study introduces a new computational technique for automatically identifying video segments containing biological locomotion. The approach is benchmarked against a conventional manual method using segment data from the existing literature, covering diverse subjects such as dogs, horses, beetles, and crickets. The results demonstrate that the new method achieves performance comparable to hand-selected clips, exhibiting high sensitivity and a strong capacity for accurate positive identification.

Optimizing power network resource allocation is a critical challenge with broad-ranging impacts. We demonstrate that key optimization issues within electrical networks can be formulated as specific instances of the Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problem, suitable for solving using both quantum and classical annealers. As a proof of concept, we applied a D-Wave quantum annealer to optimize the placement of phasor measurement units (PMUs) in the IEEE 30-bus test system. Our results, compared against solutions from a D-Wave 2000Q system and a classical annealer, highlight the value of a quantum approach in solving complex power network optimization tasks.

A primary aim of theoretical physics is to uncover the fundamental laws of nature, which are then formalized into mathematical frameworks to facilitate their practical application. This endeavor is inherently challenging, as the vast complexity of natural phenomena often obscures the distinct basic laws governing them. While advanced mathematical tools and deep physical insight can sometimes isolate these underlying principles, such qualifications are frequently scarce. Consequently, data-driven methodologies have emerged as a powerful means of extracting the essential laws governing physical systems. This article demonstrates how to derive these universal laws through symmetry and universality arguments, as well as the analysis of deviations from such laws.

This study presents a search for heavy, long-lived charged particles within the ATLAS detector at the LHC, utilizing the complete dataset of proton-proton collisions at 13 TeV collected during Run 2 (2015–2018). The analysis targets signatures of particles with high specific ionisation energy loss ($dE/d\xi$) and slow velocity ($\beta$ < 1). Data were gathered using a standard trigger configuration and an optimized tracking strategy designed for highly ionising particles, achieving an effective luminosity of 36.1 fb$^{-1}$ per inversion. The findings are compared against several Beyond Standard Model scenarios, including charged Higgs bosons, as well as Q-Kinetic Dark Matter co-annihilation models and split SUSY frameworks involving charged fermions or scalars. The results are also evaluated against hypotheses involving stable, heavy particles produced via gluon fusion or associated production with top-quarks. The analysis covers mass ranges from 100 to 2,000 GeV, finding no significant deviations from the Standard Model. Consequently, the study establishes new exclusion limits for specific theoretical frameworks, particularly in the high-mass regime, with selected cross-section upper bounds reaching down to 0.001 fb for particles with masses of 1,500 GeV.

We present near-unity on-chide collection efficiency in a chip-based single-photon solid-state quantum emitter system. By utilizing near-field characterization, we precisely mapped the emitter position relative to the nanocavity and determined its dipole orientation with nanometer-scale accuracy. These insights guided the refinement of the device geometry, resulting in an achieved figure of merit exceeding 10,000. Furthermore, by integrating this high-performance cavity with an etched optical ridge waveguide, we achieved a record-breaking 97.2% ± 2.5% collection efficiency.

The boson peak refers to a prominent feature in the low-frequency region of vibrational density of states observed in amorphous materials, which cannot be explained by a harmonic model of a continuous, homogeneous medium. This study examines the boson peak through both theoretical and experimental lenses. We propose a theoretical framework that treats an amorphous substance as a continuous homogeneous medium characterized by a frequency-dependent complex shear modulus, $G(\omega)$. Experimental support for this approach arises from various techniques, including neutron scattering. Specifically, quasi-elastic neutron scattering (QENS) probes local atomic motions on picosecond scales, whereas inelastic neutron scattering (INS) investigates the boson peak by accessing higher energy transfers. The real part of the shear modulus, $\text{Re}[G(\omega)]$, correlates with transverse acoustic phonons measured via INS, while the imaginary component, $\text{Im}[G(\omega)]$, corresponds to the longitudinal acoustic phonons detected through QENS.

The paper investigates multi-loop, multi-scale Feynman diagrams arising in the perturbative expansions of key observables, including jet cross sections, Drell-Yan processes, and Higgs production. We analyze various analytical techniques for handling such diagrams and examine their practical application through specific examples. In addition, we outline how these diagrams are evaluated using a combination of symbolic and numerical methods.

We establish a series of sum rules characterizing the $n$-th moments of eigenchannels associated with a general scattering system. These sum rules encompass the total number, total transmission count, total transmission probability, and the squared amplitudes of individual eigenchannels. Furthermore, for two-channel systems, corresponding sum rules governing the $n$-th moments of eigenvalue phases are derived. Additionally, we investigate the universality of the lower bounds observed in the first moment of eigenvalue phases.

The Far Infrared (FIR) observations from IRAS and CO spectroscopy have long identified the Far 3-kpc Arm as a prominent inter-arm structure situated roughly 10 kpc from the Galactic Center, stretching across the sky in the anti-Cygnus direction. However, recent high-resolution CO spectroscopy has revealed a complex system of multiple arms within this feature. This study presents new FIR and HI observations aimed at investigating the Far Arm's structure and kinematics. We identified a distinct component with a mean radial velocity of +60 km s$^{-1}$, located approximately 2° above the Far Arm's primary ridge. By cross-referencing CO data, we determined that this new component is superposed on the primary Far Arm, yet exhibits significantly higher excitation temperatures and lower column densities. Furthermore, we detected a clear velocity gradient along this new component, indicating it is not merely a line of sight effect but represents a separate spiral arm. Although its Galactic radius places it beyond the theoretical limit for a single-armed spiral structure, its existence suggests a possible bifurcation of the traditional Far Arm or indicates that a component of it may originate in the Galactic halo.

The field of multi-objective optimization (MOO) seeks to identify a set of non-dominated solutions that optimize multiple, often conflicting, objectives simultaneously; this collection is termed the Pareto front. In practical terms, each solution on this front represents a unique trade-off, balancing the various objectives in distinct ways. While much of the literature has focused on the efficiency of algorithms for approaching the Pareto front, less attention has been given to the diversity inherent within the resulting solution phenotypes. This study introduces a new framework for characterizing solution diversity in MOO problems and utilizes it to analyze specific multi-solution outcomes. We demonstrate that even when different algorithms find solutions covering an identical range, the phenotypic diversity associated with those solutions can differ markedly depending on the method employed.

The concept of three-dimensional (3D) matching involves pairing participants in a group so that every individual forms exactly two relationships, with the specific constraint that these two relationships do not share a second common link. We extend this framework to the **Three-Dimensional Stable Roommates Problem (3D-SRP)** by introducing binary preferences among participants, seeking 2-matches where every individual's two partners rank higher than any unconnected pair. This paper investigates the 3D-SRP within the context of **additively separable preferences**, a scenario where the desirability of any pair depends solely on the intrinsic qualities of the two individuals, excluding their identities. We establish that the total number of potential stable outcomes in 3D-SRC is bounded above by **O(n³)**, representing a substantial improvement over the exponential complexity of O(2ⁿ) found in unrestricted preferences. Furthermore, we introduce a **polynomial-time algorithm** capable of generating a complete list of all stable solutions.

In two-dimensional materials, phonon-mediated interactions are essential for establishing correlated states and facilitating phase transitions. While existing literature has concentrated on acoustic phonons responsible for ferromagnetism and valence ferroelectricity, this study investigates the effects of optical phonons on valley physics. We present a first-principles framework to compute long-range optical electron-phonon couplings, specifically targeting interlayer and intralayer mechanisms. Using kinetic theory, we calculate the finite-temperature drift-diffusion equations to model optical phonon-induced transport. Our calculations reveal that at elevated temperatures, optical phonons generate significant Hall and diffusive currents, a phenomenon supported by time-dependent simulations. Furthermore, we examine how strain influences these effects, highlighting that although optical phonons can induce long-range currents, strain remains critical for maximizing current density.

This work examines the class of metric spaces under the Gromov-Hausdorff distance, specifically focusing on elements that possess a finite center. A space qualifies as such if its Gromov-Hausdorff midpoint can be consistently defined up to a finite set of candidates. These Gromov-Hausdorff clouds are shown to be complete and possess the significant property that every subset within them exhibits a finite center as well. Furthermore, these spaces exhibit stability regarding isometric embeddings into arbitrary metric settings. The study also establishes necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of midpoints, thereby addressing partial conditions previously set forth by M. Rader in 2016. Finally, the authors present specific examples of clouds whose midpoint sets consist of exactly two elements.

This paper introduces a millimeter-wave microstrip patch antenna featuring a dual-layer feeding architecture. Utilizing two coaxial cables positioned with varying angles, this design achieves a remarkably wide impedance bandwidth of 10.6% (from 27.0 to 30.0 GHz). The antenna demonstrates dual operating modes: a traditional resonant mode excited by the primary feeding cable and a higher-order mode activated by the secondary cable. Measured results confirm an impedance bandwidth spanning 27.0 to 30.0 GHz. Additionally, the antenna supports a wide-angle scanning capability from -40° to 40°, with consistent gain performance maintained between 10.0 and 12.0 dBi.

This paper introduces a decision framework to optimize decoder performance, an essential component for fault-tolerant quantum computation relying on quantum error correction. We model the choice of decoding strategies as a Markov decision process, where an agent learns to make optimal decisions through reinforcement learning. Using the trained agent, we construct a universal decoder that operates with a constant, minimal delay. Our findings demonstrate that this reinforcement learning-based decoder attains near-optimal performance and model transferability.

Quantum metrology leverages the principles of quantum mechanics to surpass the limits inherent in classical measurement precision. However, existing quantum metrological schemes are constrained by their reliance on continuous unitary evolution, making them vulnerable to decoherence. This study introduces a quantum metrology approach that utilizes quantum jumps within a two-cavity network. By employing an input-output framework, we demonstrate that the proposed scheme can achieve an accuracy limited only by the standard quantum limit, remaining robust even under significant decoherence. This method effectively counters the vulnerabilities posed by typical metrological strategies through its resistance to substantial amounts of decoherence.

The PHENIX collaboration reports direct photon-hadron correlation measurements in Au+Au and both d+Au and p+p collisions at $\sqrt{s_{_{NN}}}=200$ MeV. In d+Au and p+p systems, correlation patterns align with expectations from cold nuclear matter models, establishing these datasets as a baseline. Conversely, in Au+Au collisions, hadron yields associated with direct photons exhibit enhanced suppression at large deflection angles compared to the d+Au reference, a signature indicative of jet-medium interactions.

In this work, we investigate the dynamics of one-dimensional fermions subject to quadratic Hamiltonians, a model significant for simulating interactions within various materials. To capture these dynamics, we introduce a digital-analog hybrid quantum computing strategy that integrates Hamiltonian decomposition with evolution operators. This method analogically emulates continuous quantum circuits, reducing the required discrete circuit depth compared to purely digital approaches. We establish a theoretical upper limit of $O(N^2)$ for circuit depth, where $N$ denotes the number of qubits, by mapping operator structures on graph states to binary tree diagrams. To verify the method's validity, we conduct numerical experiments on IBM quantum processors, focusing on simulations relevant to the BCS theory of superconductivity. These results demonstrate efficient and precise modeling of fermionic interactions, with the accuracy improving notably as the number of emulated particles increases.

Although deep neural networks are renowned for their exceptional feature extraction capabilities, their success is often hindered by the optimization-generalization dilemma, where a model achieves high training accuracy but fails to generalize well. While current research frequently targets this issue by introducing new architectural components, this paper investigates it from the perspective of feature extraction itself. Specifically, we explore whether integrating additional information into the neural network's input features can mitigate the gap between training and generalization performance. Our findings demonstrate that feeding enriched features back into the network effectively reduces this optimization-generalization gap. Furthermore, the enrichment is implemented efficiently and scalably by training a small, specialized auxiliary network alongside the main model.

Creating 3D microstructures within biological tissues is a critical area of study for life science research. While spatial light modulator (SLM) systems utilizing iterative algorithms are a common approach for this purpose, they typically require numerous iterations, thereby slowing the fabrication speed. This study introduces an advanced iterative method based on a false-lock color (FLC) model integrated with an SLM. We evaluated the FLC model's performance in generating multiple, intricate 3D structures simultaneously inside gel tissue. The findings indicate that this new approach reduces the total number of iterations needed by 90% compared to conventional techniques, resulting in a 90% increase in the rate of structure formation.
We express our gratitude for the thorough review provided by the editors and the various commenters on our paper, noting that most feedback aligns closely with our original objectives.

Monolithic CMOS sensors utilizing sensor technology on a silicon carbide substrate are anticipated to become a standard component of future high-luminosity collider experiments. To validate this approach, a 3×3 inch proof-of-concept detector named CLICTD has been developed using the small collection-electrode methodology. This design features 100 µm-thick sensors mounted on a silicon carbide substrate, where each pixel comprises a central measurement electrode surrounded by eight guard rings. This configuration enables the assessment of full depletion conditions, charge collection efficiency, and bias voltage dependencies. The study presented here compares the performance of CLICTD across different sensor thicknesses and various silicon wafers, specifically standard 4H silicon, FZ silicon, and SOI silicon, each with distinct epitaxial layer thicknesses.

The Santa Cruz Extreme Adaptive Optics Laboratory Testbed, located at Santa Cruz Mountains Observatory, offers a unique opportunity to conduct ground-based experiments in extreme adaptive optics research. Equipped with a high-power, kilowatt-class laser transmitter, this facility enables the deployment of the atmospheric self-coherence technique. This technique identifies and tracks turbulence layers by analyzing time delays between pairs of conjugate stars and their corresponding atmospheric laser speckles. By directing corrective commands toward each target layer, the system aims to equalize the intensity distribution of atmospheric laser speckles, thereby turning them into highly stable natural guide stars. This paper introduces initial experimental outcomes from the system, which integrates the Fast Atmospheric Self-Coherence Camera technique with active focal plane wavefront correction. Specifically, we demonstrate the concurrent execution of wavefront sensing and control, achieved through the synchronized operation of two wavefront sensors and two adaptive optics systems.

We introduce a new exogenous model designed to address the challenges of endogenous negative rates found in contemporary interest rate frameworks. Our proposed approach modifies the deterministic-shift extended Cox-Ingersoll-Ross (eCIR) model proposed by Duffie and Kan. The specific adjustment involves applying a negative constant to the level parameter to ensure shifts remain strictly positive. While this ensures positivity for short rates, the resulting long-term normal rate may still fall negative. We examine the probabilistic characteristics of our suggested framework and analyze its behavior under the change of measure. Furthermore, we derive the corresponding affine term structure of zero-coupon bonds and implement these findings using empirical data. Our analysis indicates that, similar to the standard extended eCIR model, the proposed model demonstrates high sensitivity to the variance parameter.

Active experiments like DUNE offer a promising avenue for detecting sterile neutrinos within energy scales of a few eV. These neutrinos could emerge from decays of light particles permitted by extensions to the Standard Model, such as the Higgs, or from the mixing of three known neutrino states. This study evaluates DUNE's ability to identify sterile neutrinos generated via the decay of a higgs-like particle with mass around 100 MeV, produced in proton-nucleus collisions. We analyze outcomes across several production mechanisms and investigate how improvements in detector resolution and fiducial volume influence detection capabilities. Additionally, we examine the constraints DUNE imposes on the mixing parameters of three-state sterile neutrinos.

Meta-analyses frequently involve studies that are not statistically independent, creating a need for cluster-robust variance estimators to address this dependency. However, such estimators demand substantial data quantities to remain reliable. This article introduces efficient implementations of these estimators utilizing the `metafor` package in R and investigates their performance through simulations. The results confirm that estimator performance improves significantly when employing an optimal, alternating variance scheme compared to traditional consistent methods. These procedures are particularly beneficial in prevalent bivariate meta-analyses, which simultaneously estimate effect sizes across two outcomes. The paper also outlines steps for calculating cluster robust variances for bivariate meta-analytic models and provides guidance on reporting these estimates within a meta-research context.

Molecular dynamics simulations of granular media are frequently constrained by graining, a problem where disparate time scales between fast wave propagation and slow external driving necessitate the use of unphysical integration steps, thereby compromising the accuracy of particle interactions. To address this, we introduce a novel multiple-time-step algorithm designed to restore accuracy by allowing integration steps to scale with the physical collision duration. By partitioning the equation of motion into fast and slow components, we employ two distinct numerical integration scales: an explicit method for the fast component and implicit integration for the slow component. Implemented within an external potential framework, this approach yields three distinct operational modes: (i) an implicit multiple-time-step algorithm utilizing variable physical time-step sizes, (ii) a scaled implicit algorithm with fixed fixed time-step sizes, and (iii) the conventional unscaled algorithm with fixed time-step sizes. We evaluate the first two approaches by examining the shear response of sheared assemblies under both quasi-static and quasi-dynamic loading conditions.

This study examines the origins of radiation in the Unruh and Hawking effects. It is demonstrated that, for a uniformly accelerated observer, radiation originates from photons present in the entire physical universe but confined to a limited segment within their local Rindler wedge, resulting from the acceleration-induced spectral distribution. Similarly, for an observer situated at a fixed finite radius around a black hole, it is shown that the associated radiation stems not from within the event horizon, but from gravitational waves generated outside it; these waves arise due to the black hole's rotation of its mass-energy, as observed by someone outside the horizon.

Using the color dipole framework, we examine how a parton's transverse momentum broadening occurs as it traverses a large nucleus. We demonstrate that even within a weakly saturated regime, this broadening aligns quantitatively with the Balitsky-Johnson prediction, which features a logarithmic dependence on the nuclear radius squared ($R_z^2$). Furthermore, we show that within the linear parton evolution framework, this mechanism can be interpreted as the absorption of two transverse gluons.
This piece presents $7^n$ distinct integer solution sets $\{(a,b)\}$ for the equation $a^2+ab+b^2=7^n$ and establishes the uniqueness of these sets.

This study examines the penetration process where a jet of liquid enters a channel and merges with a flowing stream moving in the opposite direction. The system's dynamics are modeled using the shallow flow equations, which are shown to be unstable under specific conditions. This instability triggers instabilities that generate instabilities that cause instabilities that lead to instabilities that produce instabilities that produce instabilities that produce instabilities that produce instabilities that produce instabilities that produce instabilities that lead to instabilities that produce instabilities that cause

Ensuring data integrity is a critical challenge in High-Performance Computing (HPC) as systems transition from volatile RAM to Non-Volatile Memory (NVM). Although algorithm-centric approaches offer superior restoration speeds compared to standard block-device or file-system methods, they lack the convenience of NVM-managed filesystems. This paper introduces Crash-DCU, a crash-consistent, file-system-independent algorithm designed specifically for this gap. It leverages per-object metadata and persistent write barriers, operating directly on NVM without requiring an NVM filesystem layer. The algorithm functions by maintaining a per-object state machine that tracks execution progress and ensures object states remain consistent across object boundaries. Crucially, this state machine utilizes write barriers strategically to minimize overhead while guaranteeing correctness. Our analysis demonstrates that NVM write barriers incur negligible overhead, making our solution significantly more efficient than existing algorithm-difference techniques.

Information hierarchies are essential for organizing vast datasets in fields like psychology, biology, and consumer research. Although recent advances in deep learning have enhanced the accuracy of traditional methods, they often fail to address the scalability required for massive data volumes. This work introduces a new hierarchical modeling framework that leverages deep neural networks to represent the probability distribution of a taxonomy's leaf nodes. We propose an optimized, scalable training algorithm for this framework, using approximate Bayesian computation to learn model parameters through mini-batch MCMC while employing regularized variational inference for posterior inference. Empirical evaluations on synthetic data and real-world networks demonstrate that this approach yields highly accurate leaf node classifications and scales effectively to information networks containing hundreds of thousands of nodes.

We propose a statistical framework for simulating Few-Body Dynamics based on the conservation of phase space volume. Within this approach, we analyze the evolution of Few-Body systems by examining phase functions that characterize how phase space volumes transform under coordinate changes. Applying this method to the three-body problem, we employ an iterative scheme to generate representative ensembles of initial conditions. These ensembles allow for a statistical evaluation of few-body evolution, offering a computationally efficient alternative to integrating individual trajectories. We validate this approach by contrasting our results with those from numerical integrations and by assessing prediction accuracy through various distributions of input ensembles.

This work reports a measurement of nuclear modification factors ($R_{AA}$) for nonprompt and prompt charmonium ($J/\psi$) mesons within PbPb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 5.02$ TeV, alongside comparisons to pPb and pp references. The data, gathered by the LHCb detector, utilize mesons originating from beauty hadron decays (nonprompt) and direct production (direct prompt). The obtained $R_{AA}$ measurements for nonprompt $J/\psi$ mesons across various centrality classes are consistent with those from pPb references and direct prompt $J/\psi$ mesons in pp collisions. In contrast, direct prompt $J/\psi$ mesons exhibit significant suppression in PbPb collisions, with the lowest $R_{AA}$ observed in the most central events. Furthermore, this study presents the first $R_{AA}$ measurement for nonprompt $J/\psi$ mesons in pPb collisions. The results for pPb show no significant deviation from unity, whereas PbPb collisions demonstrate significant suppression. These findings for pPb and Pbp suggest that the mechanisms driving the production of nonprompt and direct prompt $J/\psi$ mesons differ significantly.

We present a class of topoi equipped with an explicit model of continuous logic. A key benefit of this construction is the applicability of the logical subobject classifier, which facilitates the formation of topsological spaces of truth values for any statement. Furthermore, the absence of Cauchy completion in our proposed class of toposi enables the representation of statements regarding infinite size through points on the truth value topological space.

In software systems development, regression testing is essential for verifying system integrity following modifications. However, executing the entire regression test suite consumes a significant amount of time, and selecting a subset that maximizes the coverage of these selected cases is a critical goal. This study presents a method to identify a minimal subset of regression tests that covers the maximum number of chosen choices, utilizing Singular Value Decomposition (SVD). Furthermore, the proposed algorithm was parallelized to enhance processing efficiency. The strategy's efficacy was verified by evaluating the results of the system's components, and the parallel version was benchmarked against the serial implementation. Findings indicate that the system performs satisfactorily, and the parallel execution demonstrates superior performance compared to its serial counterpart.

This paper introduces a deep sequential model designed to forecast suicidal ideation by analyzing data from various formats, specifically clinical notes, electronic health records (EHR), and social media. Clinical notes are processed using pre-trained BERT, whereas social media and EHR data are handled through recurrent neural networks (RNN) and long short-term memory (LSTM) networks, respectively. These components are integrated into a unified sequence-to-sequence framework that accounts for temporal dependencies across the different data streams. The study evaluates the approach using two distinct datasets, finding that the proposed deep sequential architecture surpasses existing baselines. Additionally, the method effectively identifies specific phrases and entities most critical to predicting suicidal ideation.

Using the Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE), researchers have measured X-ray polarization for Cas A, a nearby supernova remnant, for the first time. The data were gathered over a 2.5-hour period, covering a broad energy spectrum from 10 to 12 keV. The detected source polarization degree is $2.5 \pm 0.6$ per cent, with a polarization angle of $101 \pm 10$ degrees. This angle remains constant across the observed band, though the measurement is influenced by the source's intrinsic variability. The source flux dropped by 15% between the start and end of the observation, a fluctuation that significantly impacts the uncertainty in the polarization degree. The polarization angle exhibits a systematic shift of approximately 15 degrees relative to the expected value derived from the parallax of the galactic plane, an offset that cannot be explained by systematic errors. This discrepancy is likely caused by the apparent motion of the remnant against the background star field due to proper motion, a factor that must be accounted for in future high-precision, long-duration observations.

Consider a sequence $A = \{a_1, \dots, a_n\}$ of $n$ positive integers. We define the sumset $s(A) = \{ \sum_{i \in I} a_i : I \subseteq \{1, \dots, n\} \}$, which contains all possible distinct sums formed by the elements of $A$. Erd\H{o}s conjectured that if $|s(A)| \le n + C$ for some absolute constant $C$, then $A$ must take the specific form $\{1, 2, 4, 8, \dots, 2^k, 2^k+1, \dots, 2^k+x\}$ for suitable non-negative integers $k$ and $x$. In this paper, we investigate a relaxed version of this problem by substituting the cardinality constraint with one involving the first integer. Specifically, we assume $s(A) \subseteq \{1, \dots, n+y\}$ for some constant $y$ and derive several results concerning the magnitude of $\gcd(A)$ and $a_1$. Furthermore, we propose several conjectures regarding the precise value of $\min \{a_1\}$ under these conditions.

We examine the speed of sound in dense matter within the context of the phase transition from baryonic to quark phases, which may occur in neutron stars. Our analysis shows that including strange quarks in the hadronic phase can lower the sound velocity at high densities, thereby expanding the range of the crossover region. Conversely, in the quark phase, we find that both chiral symmetry restoration and the transition away from an ideal gas behavior cause the sound velocity to rise. These effects were evaluated using various models, including the NLO chiral perturbation theory for low-density nuclear matter, the Walecka model, and the Bag Model. We further calculated the sound velocity across the full equation of state to assess neutron star stability against radial oscillations, utilizing the criteria for barotropic stability established by Glendenning.

The compass state, a highly squeezed coherent state, is a non-classical light source capable of surpassing the standard quantum limit in precision measurements. This study examines how displacement and squeezing parameters influence the state's properties within the Fock space. We demonstrate that varying these parameters significantly alters the state's photon-number distribution, mean photon count, photon bunching behavior, and uncertainty product. Consequently, the state exhibits greater nonclassicality when its first-order coherence function $|g^{(1)}(0)|$ approaches zero, a condition that can be achieved through specific adjustments of the squeezing and displacement variables.

This paper presents a novel methodology for characterizing multiphase flow interfaces, utilizing skeleton generation and analysis. The proposed technique is streamlined, model-agnostic, and applicable to both experimental data and simulations. It extracts interface features by applying a level set function to the phase segmentation, from which a skeleton is generated by locating and reducing the function's zero-level set. The zero-level set is then width-calculated by performing a level set function on the skeleton, and width-calculation involves performing a distance transformation on the zero-level set. The resulting skeleton is subsequently analyzed by identifying and removing spurious branches, narrowing narrowed segments, and isolating terminal nodes. Finally, branching topology is defined by the removal process, and narrowed regions are analyzed to derive width metrics, such as their distribution. The methodology's efficacy is demonstrated through two case studies: analyzing branching in rising gas bubbles and assessing foam structure, including bubble size characterization, within a bubble column.

Recent studies have revealed that the giant viruses Mimivirus and M2-490, each comprising over 1,000 amino acids, exhibit self-rolling behavior. This study investigates the mechanical forces governing this phenomenon, modeling the viruses as cylindrical structures where intermolecular interactions between side chains and the viral membrane dictate the length of loops formed by hairpin turns. We demonstrate that when these loops are regulated by a specific critical hairpin length, the system undergoes periodic rolling driven by hairpin formation and breaking. Furthermore, we show that the distance traveled by a virus is directly proportional to the average hairpin length. While the initial driving mechanism originates from loop relaxation, we present evidence that this process transitions into true self-rolling when the driving force is modified to account for virus-membrane friction and viscosity. Ultimately, our findings suggest that self-rolling offers an advantageous mechanism for viral transport across cellular membranes.

U-type warped disk galaxies are thought to result from tidal interactions with their surrounding environment. In this study, we investigate U-type warps in SFKGS (a sample of 1,100 galaxies with stellar mass greater than $10^{10.25} M_{\odot}$) that are also classified as jellyfish galaxies—defined by the presence of tidal tails extending from the galaxy's disk. We detected warps in 11% of the jellyfish galaxies within our catalog. For these warped systems, the warp angle ($\theta_{\rm warp}$) and the ratio of warp to warp ($\rm{W_{\rm{W}}}$) were determined using the $G_{\rm{W}}$ index and the $G_{\rm{W}}$ index, respectively. We observed that jellyfish galaxies exhibit more severe warps compared to non-tail-bearing galaxies, evidenced by a higher median $\rm{W_{\rm{W}}}$ ratio of 0.08 versus 0.04. Additionally, the distribution of warp angles indicates that jellyfish galaxies possess more significant warps, with a median angle of 13.8° compared to 9.2° in non-tail populations. The relationship between warp severity and specific projected tidal tail length ($L_{\rm{W}}$) was analyzed, revealing a positive correlation: galaxies with longer tidal tails generally exhibit stronger war

This work examines gradient shrinking Ricci solitons containing a Liouville theorem for bounded harmonic functions that possess a Liouville scalar curvature. We can demonstrate that any such soliton of this nature must exhibit uniform (constant) Ricci curvature. As a direct application, we derive a corresponding change of coordinate theorem.

In the study of phonon topological insulators, significant progress has been made in systems lacking local inversion symmetry but possessing time-reversal symmetry. However, achieving this condition in crystalline lattices with high crystallographic symmetry remains difficult. This work demonstrates that in cubic $A$Bi$_2$ ($A$=K, Rb, Cs) Laves phases, chiral phonon modes emerge within a limited region of the phonon dispersion zone. These modes arise because local inversion symmetry is broken at specific Bi-Bi bonds, which causes an energy splitting of anti-crossing phonon branches. Consequently, these phonons exhibit one-way propagation confined to narrow paths, with their count determined by a local topological invariant. Furthermore, we predict that introducing defects or narrow channels within the Bi layers can induce one-way surface modes. Ultimately, these findings offer a viable strategy for generating chiral phonons in cubic lattice structures.

In insulating materials, Born effective charges quantify the anomalous displacement of atoms induced by external electric fields; in conductors, their analogous counterparts for semimetals and metals are computed via ab initio methods as Anadibatic (nonadiabatic) effective charges. These charges represent the displacement of a test particle carrying a specified effective charge under adiabatic conditions. This study examines the Drude weight—a metric of perfect conductivity linked to the acceleration of charges—within a simplified 1D model system and contrasts these findings with *ab initio* calculations of the Drude weight and effective charges in aluminum. We demonstrate that the magnitude of the Drude weight correlates with the ratio of the average effective mass to the average absolute value of the nonadiabatic effective charge.

This study examines how thermal fluctuations influence incompressible fluid turbulence, a topic that has remained largely unexplored since the pioneering work of Landau and Lifshichi nearly a century ago. By applying a fully non-perturbative renormalization group method, we determine the exact fixed point governing incompressible turbulent dynamics. Our analysis reveals that the system behaves as a stable, Gaussian process characterized by a single, minute nontrivial exponent, $ \epsilon = (\bar{4} - d)/d $, where $ d $ represents spatial dimension. This finding confirms and quantifies Landau's conjecture regarding the scaling of energy spectral density, $ E(k) \sim k^{-2} (1 + k^2 \ell_B^2)^{- (1 - \epsilon)/2} $, with $ \ell_B $ representing the Buchholtz length scale. Furthermore, our results indicate that for dimensions $ d \ge 3 $, the influence of thermal noise on fluid energy transport is negligible.

The response of three-dimensional topological insulators to coupled electric and magnetic fields is examined, revealing a novel term proportional to the product of two field strengths. This finding corroborates the theoretical prediction made by Xiao, Wang, and others in 2010. We further analyze the relationship between this term and half-integer quantum Hall conductance, as well as connections to surface charge fractionalization (Witten effect) and bulk charge fractionalization (half-integer quantum Hall effect). Ultimately, these phenomena indicate a fundamental distinction between 3D topological insulators and 2D topological insulators.

The study investigates a standard linear delay system defined by $\dot{x}(t) = -x(t) + u(t-\tau)$, where the input $u$ is a chaotic time series and the system is subjected to a time-varying delay $\tau(t)$. We demonstrate that this variable delay can induce substantial improvements in the input series' diffusion. Specifically, when the current delay value is significantly longer than the characteristic delay scale of the system, the system's behavior becomes dominated by this larger timescale. We introduce a simplified model that accurately captures the essential dynamics of the system under these extended delay conditions. Furthermore, we analyze how the variable delay impacts the fractal dimension of the resulting chaotic output, showing it can rise sharply. Numerical results reveal that systems with modulated delays exhibit a "giant enhancement" in fractal dimension, increasing up to 100% beyond baseline levels.

While modern software engineering practices increasingly utilize data to support decision-making, the engineering design process itself remains underexploited as a source of mining opportunities. This research introduces a methodology for extracting and analyzing design discussions through both visual and textual formats. The visual component encompasses the evolution of decisions across multiple diagrams, whereas the textual aspect captures the full breadth of design conversations. A key decision-making framework is established to represent choices using decision records, ensuring stability of these records over time by linking them to corresponding text. Furthermore, a decision stability metric is defined and demonstrated through a case study involving the analysis of over 1,000 decision records from UML diagrams and their associated discussions within the UMAP tool.

We hypothesize that post-inflation gravity arises retro-causally from a vacuum state in which space-time exhibits a macro-quantum-coherent, retro-causal holographic structure. In this framework, universal gravity emerges due to the collective coupling between matter fields and coherent zero-point fluctuations. This model explains the association between geometric area and entropy as deriving from the quantum, coherent, holographic nature of the underlying vacuum. Furthermore, we propose that space-time geometry emerges dynamically from the coherent interactions of these zero-point fluctuations with universal, universal Higgs and Goldstone fields. Specifically, coherent potentials within these fields trigger a mechanism analogous to the Aharonov-Bohm effect, manifesting as causal loops that drive holographic time reversal. This retro-causality is suggested as the fundamental source of both area-proportional entropy and time reversal itself.

Proximity algorithms are widely used to identify minimizers of sum-type functions involving smooth and smoothable components, while a new class of such functions recently gained prominence through the addition of third smooth components. This study introduces a unified proximal-gradient framework applicable across scenarios with two or three smooth parts, achieving linear convergence rates. Notably, a specific choice of parameters within this general method yields standard proximal-gradient techniques and their variants for both existing and newly defined function classes. Leveraging this broad convergence result, the work further develops accelerated variants that ensure rapid convergence for problem categories supporting strong convexity.

This study introduces the concept of weakly 1-absorbing prime ideals within the context of commutative rings with a multiplicative structure. Several properties are examined, along with the discussion of related notions such as weakly absoring primes. The paper further presents specific examples to clarify these concepts and establishes the characterization of such ideals in polynomial rings.

This study reports the most recent findings on the semileptonic $B \to \rho \ell \nu_\ell$ decays ($\ell = e, \mu$) derived from the $ee^-$ dataset collected by the Belle experiment at SuperKEKB between 2019 and 2021. The analysis targets the specific $\rho$ decay channels $\rho \to K^0_S \pi^\pm$ and $\rho \to K^+ \pi^\mp$, selecting signal events through a likelihood fit applied to the invariant mass distribution of the recoil system against the $\rho$ candidate. By employing this technique, we have generated differential branching fraction measurements across the $q^2$ range of 8 to 22 $\text{GeV}^2/c^2$ for both channels. These results are compared against prior differential $q^2$ bins and aggregated over the $q^2$ spectrum to determine the absolute branching fractions. Furthermore, we evaluate the absolute branching fractions alongside previous differential results in $q^2$ to establish a world average for $B \to \rho \ell \nu_\ell$ decays across all lepton flavors.

The development of ever-more powerful spectroscopic techniques is essential for addressing pressing astrophysical challenges, particularly as the astrophastical community seeks to validate the cosmological model through precise measurements of the Hubble constant ($H_0$) and the matter density parameter ($\Omega_m$). These critical insights are largely derived from the "baryon acoustic oscillation" (BAO) signal embedded within the large-scale distribution of galaxies. The upcoming Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) will harness the redshift spectral cross-correlation method to access this signal, a strategy that demands high-precision wavelength calibration. We demonstrate that the desert of detector response in the vicinity of the red $H\alpha$ line offers an ideal internal calibration reference, provided the astrophastical community creates robust systems to exploit it. We present two novel on-detector calibration approaches that leverage this line and are fully compatible with DESI's operational workflow. Furthermore, we show that these methods can dramatically enhance current calibration strategies, substantially reducing residual systematic errors.

This research introduces a comprehensive survey of deep learning methodologies for predicting molecular pair interactions, addressing key questions regarding the representation of drug pairs, the modeling of inter-molecular features, and how these approaches compare. Additionally, we deliver an extensive evaluation of state-of-the-art models using the most current benchmark, which reveals that the best existing models achieve only limited success. To address these shortcomings, we propose a new model that achieves superior performance compared to existing methods while maintaining simplicity and interpretability. Finally, we examine interpretability techniques for relation prediction and propose new strategies to further clarify model decisions.

Identifying road damage is critical for maintaining road networks and ensuring traffic safety. While previous research has primarily depended on expert assessments or on-board sensor systems, this study introduces a novel, cost-effective approach leveraging street-view imagery. By leveraging transfer learning, the methodology utilizes a pre-trained ResNet101 model, adapting it for multiple nations. Trained exclusively on damage images from Germany, the system demonstrates strong generalization capabilities, accurately detecting road defects in South Korea and the United States with high precision. The achieved F1-scores were 0.9355 for Germany, 0.8811 for South Korea, and 0.8611 for the United States.

Imitation learning aims to derive an agent's goal from expert demonstrations, yet current methods typically depend on full-state observations that are often unavailable in real-world scenarios. To address this limitation, we propose a novel approach that enables the extraction of objective goals from partial agent perceptions. By integrating an intrinsic motivation mechanism with a hierarchical policy, our method effectively models complex, long-horizon tasks. Additionally, we developed a rigorous theoretical framework to demonstrate that the hierarchical method optimally approximates the intrinsic goals within the Markov partition induced by the agent's observation space. Empirical evaluations across two real environments confirm that our algorithm significantly surpasses existing solutions, especially when expert access to the complete state is denied to the agent.

A critical unresolved issue regarding the formation of the first stars is the mechanism regulating the accretion rate of Population III protostars. In this study, we investigate the interaction between a Population III protostar and the surrounding accretion disk using 3D magnetohydrodynamic simulations. Our results indicate that even a weak seed magnetic field in the disk, coupled with the magnetorotational instability (MRI), undergoes significant amplification by factors of $10^2$ to $10^3$ due to the rapid differential rotation characteristic of Population III disks. This intense magnetic activity subsequently generates a strong stellar wind, which strips magnetic flux from the disk interior. Consequently, the MRI is quenched, preventing the fragmentation that typically leads to lower accretion rates. This regulatory process maintains a high, constant mass accretion rate throughout the star's growth.

Association rules are frequently employed to uncover intricate patterns within tabular datasets. While rule redundancy can hinder their interpretability, numerous strategies have been developed to filter out superfluous associations. This study introduces a new approach for achieving this denoising by (1) defining multiple categories of redundant rules and (2) outlining three algorithms that deduce rules across three of these specific redundancy types. Redundancy definitions rely on three fundamental deduction schemes; consequently, the deduction schemes are also categorized and renamed to reflect their underlying principles. Furthermore, the paper addresses the challenge of compactness by focusing on minimum-size bases for each redundancy category. Although bases consisting of fewest rules have long been recognized as an effective way to enhance interpretation, existing research on minimum-size bases addresses only global redundancy. Our work extends this concept by addressing the minimum-size bases for three additional redundancy categories for the first time.

Individuals within the criminal justice system frequently encounter mental disorders, and recent research indicates that mandating mental health treatment for convicted offenders can reduce recidivism. This study investigates the impact of such treatment by examining 1,100 inmates in a single Midwestern state who were required to enroll in mental health programs post-conviction. Using a difference-in-differences approach, the analysis compares recidivism rates between mandated participants and a control group of non-participants. Results reveal that mandated individuals experience lower recidivism rates at both 1-year and 2-year intervals post-release compared to the control group. Furthermore, the study assesses the impact of treatment intensity on outcomes, finding that those who completed more treatment sessions demonstrate significantly reduced recidivism than those who completed fewer sessions or dropped out.

This research introduces parameterized variations of generalized Apostol–Bernoulli polynomials alongside their corresponding generating functions, examines various properties and relationships within these polynomials, and establishes connections with additional special polynomial families.

Radio maps are increasingly vital for next-generation wireless networks, particularly in supporting mission-critical services like autonomous driving and drone delivery. Their ability to visualize how radio signals propagate across a geographic area makes them invaluable for offloading data and managing interference. However, acquiring these maps in real-world scenarios often incurs high costs and complexity, especially when relying on manual measurement equipment operated by humans. This paper introduces a fully autonomous framework for radio map estimation utilizing unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). The system leverages low-cost sensors to capture essential data for channel modeling, including orientation, position, sensor readings, and channel state information. A novel two-stage approach is employed: the UAV autonomously explores the environment to gather data, followed by an offline channeled modeling process that accounts for the aircraft's dynamic movements. This separation optimizes both map exploration efficiency and channel estimation accuracy. Experimental validation was conducted in an indoor setting of $10 \times 10 \times 3$ meters using a $900$ MHz channel. Results demonstrate that the proposed autonomous scheme achieves performance on par with traditional human-operated methods.

This study introduces HMM-based anomaly detection, a novel approach for identifying irregularities in sequential time-series data. The proposed method is particularly effective for sequences exhibiting strong temporal dependencies, leveraging the forward-backward algorithm to efficiently calculate HMM sequencing probabilities. By comparing a target sequence against established normal models, the technique identifies segments that deviate from expected patterns. The authors present a specific four-state HMM developed for normal human gait data, utilizing it to detect non-walking activities such as arm swinging or running. Validated through experiments on this dataset, the results demonstrate the method's high precision in identifying unusual activities.

Multimodal person verification has emerged as a critical research area, driven by the ability to combine multiple data sources to surpass the limitations inherent in single modality systems. This study investigates three distinct modalities—audio, visual, and thermal—for person verification tasks. We present a comprehensive dataset comprising over 1,000 subjects, annotated for various modalities, along with an evaluation framework to test performance. Our initial analysis reveals that while audio and visual features yield similar results, thermal features demonstrate superior efficacy. Furthermore, we evaluate several state-of-the-art fusion techniques, finding that early fusion methods outperform both single modalities and late fusion approaches, thereby achieving the highest verification accuracy.

Data augmentation is a method for enhancing model performance by generating additional synthetic training samples, which is particularly vital for developing Large-Scale Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) and Machine Translation (MT) systems. However, creating augmented speech data is often expensive and computationally demanding, involving complex audio manipulations like time stretching, pitch shifting, and phoneme-level alignment. This study introduces a straightforward augmentation technique that requires little computation and no audio manipulation, functioning by pairing existing translation alignments with the phoneme sequences of speech to form new training instances. We demonstrate that this approach yields improvements across ASR and MT tasks and achieves results comparable to, or even superior to, augmentation strategies that involve intricate audio processing.

We introduce a broad maximum likelihood estimator (MLE) for the mixture's mean parameter and demonstrate that it possesses strong asymptotic properties. Specifically, we prove consistency and normality under the general scenario and subsequently derive an asymptotically valid standard error. Leveraging these findings, we develop a broad class of sampling schemes and establish that the corresponding MLEs are also consistent and normal while near-optimal confidence intervals (CIs) with precise coverage probabilities are achievable.

Ensuring privacy is a critical concern in the age of big data. One-sided Differential Privacy (ODLDP), a specialized form of this concept, was created to protect binary private attributes protected by data linkage with public demographic data. This study quantifies the total count of reveals that occur, considering both direct exposure and indirect exposure caused by statistical dependencies. We established both sufficient and necessary conditions for direct exposure. Additionally, we derived the optimal mechanism for direct exposure that minimizes the probability of exposure. For indirect exposure, we developed a method to estimate an upper bound on the number of exposures. Numerical simulations were conducted to evaluate the performance of proposed approaches.

This study investigates gas composition in the outer regions of the protoplanetary disk around AS 209 by analyzing ALMA observations of $^{12}$CO, $^{13}$CO, and C$^{18}$O at an angular resolution of 0.25" ($\sim$100 AU). The data reveal a significant gap in relative $^{12}$CO emission between 50 and 100 AU, which is also present in $^{13}$CO emission. Conversely, $^{13}$CO and C$^{18}$O emissions remain uniform across this zone, showing no such gaps. Two primary hypotheses are evaluated to explain this disparity: radial freeze-out of $^{12}$CO and radial variations in chemical processing. The observed abundance ratios ($^{12}$CO/$^{13}$CO $\sim$10 and $^{13}$CO/$^{18}$CO $\sim$10) align with interstellar medium (ISM) values, suggesting the disk shares ISM-like initial ratios. Furthermore, the ratio of $^{12}$CO/$^{13}$CO drops sharply within 100 AU, consistent with freeze-out mechanisms. We establish the presence of "mild" solutions for a first-order control-based Mean Field Game under constraints requiring that state trajectories remain within a closed and bounded subset of Euclidean space. A distinguishing aspect of this study is the incorporation of control measures possessing zero Lebesgue density, a scenario that significantly complicates the associated Hamiltonian and the associated dynamic boundary conditions. To navigate these complexities, we reformulate the problem equivalently as a system of coupled partial differential equations featuring constraints on the measures. Leveraging this representation, we prove the existence of solutions by combining the theory of monotone operator with the Schauder fixed point theorem.

Recent research has revealed numerous linear alignments of stars within the Milky Way, initially hypothesized to represent orbits around unseen, massive structures. However, the current study reveals that the majority of these apparent "strings" are merely coincidental projections of stars situated at vastly different distances, a conclusion reached by re-examining data from the Gaia mission. Furthermore, the evidence suggests that even the most prominent and previously cited stellar strings are likely chance alignments rather than physical associations.

Visual style compatibility assessment is a critical component in e-commerce, yet existing deep learning approaches often yield unsatisfactory outcomes. Addressing this, we introduce VICTOR (Visual INcompatibility Detection with ORansformer), a novel end-to-end deep metric learning framework designed to predict compatibility between a pair of garments. To enhance model performance, we employ a domain-specific pre-training strategy using an image encoder tailored to detect visual features pertinent to fabric and fabric compatibility. Empirical results demonstrate that this pre-training approach yields significant improvements over generic models trained on large-scale datasets. Furthermore, leveraging the Transformer architecture allows the system to effectively capture long-range dependencies within garment images, yielding additional gains in the compatibility assessment task.

Quantum resource theory serves as a rigorous framework for quantifying nonclassicality and entanglement, evaluating quantum correlations, and determining the distinguishability between various quantum states. This introductory survey examines resource theories applied to generalized nonclassical light, focusing on pure and mixed states as well as operations and measurements. We analyze the most common resource models, which include super-semeness, entanglement, coherence, and magic, and discuss their respective "free" sets. Additionally, we investigate applications of these frameworks in characterizing light generation, manipulation, and detection methods, as well as experimental verification. The discussion extends to the utility of these theories in understanding quantum advantage within imaging and beyond, highlighting their relevance beyond foundational physics into broader technological contexts.

This paper investigates the convergence behavior of buffered asynchronous server algorithms in distributed deep learning frameworks. We demonstrate that without imposing constraints on the maximum delay or assuming bounded gradients, global convergence to an $\epsilon$-stationary point of the global model can be achieved. Specifically, under conditions of limited delay, the proposed buffered asynchronous method requires $O(\frac{L^2 D \sigma^2}{\epsilon^2})$ communication rounds, where $L$ represents the Lipschitz constant of the loss function, $D$ denotes the maximum number of local iterations, and $\\sigma$ is the variance of stochastic gradients. This represents a substantial improvement over existing methods for this problem type, offering an asymptotic communication advantage of an order of magnitude. Furthermore, we propose a novel method to rigorously bound the Lipschitz constant for neural network loss functions, providing sharper convergence guarantees.

This study introduces a functional calculus based on a countable collection of generators of contraction semigroups, which are assumed to be continuous in the strong topology. The symbol algebra adopted for this framework comprises polynomial tempered distributions. The paper establishes a differentiable property of the resulting calculus and elucidates its range through the utilization of the polynomial shift commutant. An illustrative application involves determining a functional of an unbounded array of second-order derivative operators.

We investigate the fraction of dark matter that could be constituted by primordial black holes (PBHs) of various masses, leveraging recent constraints from the Gaia mission on horizontal-branch star accelerations and employing an enhanced application of swampland conjectures. Our analysis indicates that if an extra dimension, shielded by a specific scale, exists as predicted by string theory, the maximum proportion of dark matter that can be PBHs is significantly reduced. This upper limit is further tightened by imposing the Planckian curvature conjecture and by considering the recent de Sitter swampland conjecture. Consequently, our findings offer fresh perspectives on the de Sitter conjecture and its ramifications for dark matter composed of PBHs.

This study investigates the dynamics of floating rafts featuring sharp discontinuities in thickness, representing a specific type of viscoelastic viscid fluid. The mathematical framework employs the free-surface incompressible Stokes equations alongside a free-surface jump condition for stress, which is formulated using the asymptotic method of Ben-David and Liron (2012). The analysis reveals that a raft discontinuity generates a characteristic flow pattern where the material decelerates ahead of the raft segment and accelerates behind it. The study also identifies the emergence of a surface rift—a thin zone of high shear strain—behind the discontinuity. The work quantifies raft deformation and segment rotation as a consequence of these forces. Furthermore, the conditions under which these flows induce buckling deformations on the raft surface are derived. The resulting numerical simulations are compared against experimental observations from previous research.

This study investigates the influence of uniaxial strain on the structural and electronic characteristics of wurtzite Ga$N$, utilizing density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Results indicate that compressive strain along the c-axis and tensile strain along the a-axis both narrow the bandgap energy. Notably, uniaxial tensile strain along the a-axis enhances in-plane hole mobility by up to 100 times compared to the unstressed state, reaching a maximum of 1000 cm$^2$ V$^{-1}$ s$^{-1}$ under 1.5% strain. This significant mobility increase stems from strain-induced shifts in valence-band maximum positions and reduced effective hole masses. To facilitate large-scale production of such strained Ga$N$ films, we identified ZnGeN$_2$ and MgSiN$_2$ as optimal lattice-matching substrates, offering mismatch values below 0.3%.

We introduce a Temporal Difference (TD) learning approach designed to estimate the optimal navigation policy for marine robots, leveraging Gaussian Process models to represent unknown environmental dynamics. Addressing the computational intractability of standard GPs on large datasets, we integrate a SPaSe kernel to enable efficient sparse GP regression and utilize only the inducing points as data. Furthermore, we apply the GP posterior to calculate a posterior mean for the policy's optimal value function within the TD framework. Since deriving the exact posterior variance is computationally prohibitive, we approximate this term by linearly combining the prior GP variance with the temporal delta (TD) error. The resulting policy, determined by minimizing estimated exploration–exploitation uncertainty, is updated iteratively. Empirical evaluations conducted on both simulated and real-world underwater navigation scenarios demonstrate that the proposed SPaSe GP TD algorithm significantly outperforms existing methods by delivering quicker convergence and higher sample efficiency.

We define a Darboux transform and a real-analytic characterization for a gauge transformation of isothermic surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^3$ that involves a specific conformal factor defined by the pullback of a quadratic differential from $\mathbb{R}^3$ minus a discrete set of poles located on the surface. Applying this framework to each component of the formula, we derive numerous examples of isothermic surfaces not previously known, particularly by utilizing the theory of algebraic curves and their Jacobians to construct globally meromorphic pulls back quadratic differentials. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these Darboux transforms can be understood as special instances within a broader class of isothermic surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^3$ where the associated quadratic differential exhibits local behavior modeled on a local Calapso transformation.
