Preferential sweeping, the process where heavy inertial particles accumulate in low-strain regions within turbulent flows, plays a critical role in atmospheric turbulence. This phenomenon is vital for understanding the settling of snow, which poses significant hazards to aviation safety. This study utilizes high-speed video to capture the dynamics of settling snow within a wind tunnel, revealing that snowflakes exhibit preferential sweeping. The evidence suggests this effect is driven by snowflakes' high inertia and negative buoyancy. Furthermore, the research indicates that turbulent kinetic energy dissipation rates are significantly impacted by snow settling, with these impacts becoming more pronounced as snowfall intensity increases.

Active inference is a theoretical framework that explains how biological systems navigate and behave within their environments. In this study, we present a new approach to active inference that employs deep learning techniques to encode representations of the world model, thereby removing the need for hand-crafted state encodings typically required by existing methods. Evaluated on a robot navigation task, our method demonstrates its ability to automatically generate hierarchical policies that enable an agent to explore its environment and locate a designated goal.

Addressing the critical challenges of massive data generation and storage in large-scale detector experiments, this paper introduces a dual-functioning data compression framework based on a bicephalous autoencoder. The proposed system employs a symmetric architecture utilizing fully connected layers at its extremes and convolutional layers in the core, featuring separate inference and encoding branches. During operation, the inference segment extracts high-level features from input data, while the encoding segment translates these specific features into a compressed representation. This mechanism effectively harnesses intrinsic data correlations to facilitate significant reduction in file dimensions. Validation using the ATMO 3D sparse tomographic dataset demonstrates an almost 50-fold compression ratio with negligible loss in reconstructive quality.

The Finini gravity model, a novel modification of general relativity, posits that gravitational interactions weaken at large scales. Within this theoretical framework, the paper examines the statistical properties of the Milky Way's dark matter halo. The analysis indicates that the transition from isothermal profiles to NFW profiles can be successfully explained by Finini gravity. The statistical parameters of dark matter halos are derived using the generalized gamma distribution, a choice that offers greater flexibility than the standard gamma distribution. Furthermore, the ratio of the maximum radius to the scale radius ($R_{\text{max}}/R_s$) follows a log-normal distribution. The study concludes by contrasting the results with previous research on the same topic.

A subset collection $\mathcal{F}$ of $d$-dimensional convex polytopes in $\mathbb{R}^d$, each with exactly $d+1$ vertices, forms a convex geometric hypergraph. This structure $\mathcal{F}$ is considered uniform if every polytopet includes precisely $s$ elements. For any given integer $n$, the saturation number $sat(n,\mathcal{F})$ denotes the maximum count of pairs that can be added to $\mathcal{F}$ such that adding any additional valid pair would force the creation of an isomorphic pair; consequently, $sat(n,\mathcal{F})$ represents $| \mathcal{F}| + n - 1$. This study establishes that for sufficiently large dimensions $d$, the count $sat(n,\mathcal{F})$ scales proportionally to $n^{d-1}$, thereby generalizing prior work by Frankl and R\"odl [1989] on standard $k$-uniform hypergraphs where $n$ is large.

This study examines the differential cross-sections for angular alpha production in the $^{6}$Li($^{51}$V,$\alpha$)$^{52}$Cr reaction at 20 MeV, analyzing data through 2022 using the Cluster-Preformed Resonance Model (CPRM). The theoretical predictions align well with experimental results, demonstrating strong concordance. The resonance states of the $^{6}$Li-$^{51}$V compound nucleus were further investigated, with calculations yielding reduced widths that match experimental data. Additionally, spectroscopic amplitudes for $^{6}$Li decaying into $\alpha$ and $^{3}$He were computed and compared favorably to prior measurements.

This paper presents a Pacific lamprey-inspired climbing robot designed to replicate the adhesive locomotion of its biological counterpart. The system utilizes a multi-material 3D printing technique to fabricate an adhesive pad that mimics the lamprey's ventral suction cup, enabling strong adhesion on both glass and metal surfaces. The robot's actuation mechanism emulates lampreyn's undulatory movement through a climbing strategy adapted from observed animal behaviors. A key innovation is the use of a visual feedback loop to automate this complex motion, achieved by detecting surface features via an onboard camera and a linear feature detector. Experimental trials validate the robot's load-bearing capacity of 1.5 times its weight and demonstrate successful traversal of 2 meters, confirming both the effectiveness of the hybrid manufacturing method and the robustness of the visual-based control system.

This paper introduces a novel, data-driven methodology for crafting optimal personalized treatments by integrating machine learning with a stochastic tumor-immune interaction Fokker-Planck (FP) model. Unlike previous LP-based optimization approaches that rely on a single, population-wide FP equation, our strategy derives a dedicated FP model for each patient using high-dimensional clinical data. This individualized modeling enables the generation of tailored therapy plans, and the framework successfully produces robust treatment recommendations when applied to real-world colon-cancer datasets.

This study addresses the scheduling challenge in decentralized Device-to-Device (D2D) environments, aiming to schedule transmission queues that minimize a weighted combination of Age of Information (AoI) and transmission delay. Given the prohibitive computational complexity of the corresponding optimization problem, the authors introduce a dual-decomposition framework that breaks the task into single-link subproblems. These links are then solved using an AoI-aware backpressure strategy. Subsequently, the individual link scheduling decision is refined via a deep learning approach to mitigate residual performance gaps. Finally, the proposed learning-driven scheduler is executed in a simulation setting to demonstrate its superior performance when benchmarked against conventional dual-based and backpressure-only methodologies.

This paper establishes a partial strong solution for the 3D compressible Euler equations, assuming initial data with small enstrophy and large mean specific entropy that varies slowly. By leveraging energy estimates, which provide only weak regularity for the vorticity, the authors derive an $L^2$ estimate for the vorticity gradient. This intermediate estimate suffices to validate the applicability of an existing approximation of the material derivative, thereby confirming the preservation of helicity throughout the evolution.

Building on the work presented in \cite{KochTao2003}, this study examines how the Fourier transforms of data behave when integrated over large frequencies in connection with the one-dimensional complete smoothness requirement for the $k$-th order Zakharov-Lew-Weaver (DLS) equations. Specifically within this analysis, for sufficiently large $|k|$, it is demonstrated that if the initial conditions possess a finite $L^2$ norm, then the corresponding reflection coefficient for the linearized DLS system must exhibit a decay of $O(k^{-\frac{1}{4}})$. This finding significantly improves upon the previously established bound of $O(k^{-\frac{1}{2}})$. Furthermore, it is proven that when $|k| \geq 3$, the smallness threshold for the norm of the data can be elevated to include functions with finite $L^2$ derivatives of all orders, thereby enhancing the known results regarding large $|k|$ obtainable by Gustafsson, Takaoka, and Masaki \cite{GustafssonTakaokaMasaki2005}.

Post-Newtonian (PN) theory predicts that eccentricities persist in the late inspiral phase of compact binary systems within a geodesic, test-particle limit around a Schwarzschild spacetime. This study derives precise estimates of late inspiral residual eccentricity applicable to the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) threshold of gravitational-wave detectors. By employing an adaptive time integration scheme, we numerically evaluate the balance between radial and tangential components of the inspiral velocity at the largest orbital radius considered for a given eccentricity and SNR threshold. Our derived velocity conditions are contrasted against circular inspiral criteria, offering a simplified method for calculating residual eccentricity. Furthermore, these conditions inform the comparison of eccentricity evolution across different orders of Post-Newtonian theory, specifically from 3.5PN to 5.5PN.

Event detection is a fundamental task in many real-world graph applications, including identifying sudden traffic congestion, spotting anomalies in communication networks, and locating disease outbreaks. Although deep learning has significantly advanced this field, most existing methods rely on static graphs, overlooking the evolving structures that arise from dynamic node interactions. Furthermore, current approaches often struggle with data sparsity, which occurs when events are rare and imbalanced. To overcome these limitations, this study introduces Graph WaveNet, a new deep learning framework that integrates multi-scale wavelets with graph convolutional networks. By utilizing multi-scale wavelets to extract time-frequency features, Graph WaveNet effectively captures patterns at various durations, including the detection of sudden occurrences. Simultaneously, the graph convolutional networks component models the topological structure to account for heterogeneous relationships between nodes. Additionally, to address the challenge of sparsity, the framework employs a negative sampling strategy to mitigate class imbalance. Extensive experiments across three real-world datasets demonstrate that Graph WaveNet outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in both accuracy and robustness. This work examines the resolution of the Guderley implosion shock challenge within a polytropic medium of uniform density, utilizing the boundary condition imposed by the gauge group. The entanglement between shock geometry and the internal structure of the underlying fluid is explored, revealing a discrete set of viable solutions where each corresponds to a specific dynamical scale. By applying entanglement theory to fluid dynamics, we identify this phenomenon as an analog of topological confinement. The impact of internal angular momentum on shock structure is also analyzed, showing that it necessitates a reduction in the effective polytropic index experienced by the external shock wave. Furthermore, we investigate how non-uniform density gradients modify shock behavior, specifically by considering a power-law profile $\rho(x) \propto |x|^\nu$; in this context, we determine the precise set of self-similar solutions and delineate the conditions under which the shock remains trapped in contact with the center.

In recent times, the opacity of many machine learning and artificial intelligence systems has fueled the adoption of Explainable AI (XAI). While XAI techniques are capable of generating human-comprehensible explanations for an system's predictions, the specific needs of end-users often remain unclear. To address this gap, this paper proposes a user-centric approach designed to capture the explanation requirements crucial for building trustworthy AI. Functioning as a subset of the broader requirements engineering process, this methodology facilitates the articulation of what users need to know to trust and accept AI outcomes. Utilizing input from a diverse stakeholder group, the paper presents the developed method through a practical application within the cancer cancer diagnosis context. Finally, the discussion outlines potential future enhancements and avenues for further investigation regarding the presented approach.

Classifying colorectal polyps and assessing their dysplastic potential are critical tasks for pathologists, as they aid in early cancer detection and prevention through timely screening. However, the manual nature of these evaluations is prone to variability and inconsistency. To support advancements in computer-aided diagnostics, we introduce **UniToPatho**, a dataset comprising 1,000 histopathological images of colorectal polyps captured at 20× magnification. These images are meticulously categorized into normal or neoplastic cases and, for neoplastic samples, assigned to one of three dysplasia grades: mild, moderate, or severe. To enhance annotation precision, a two-stage process was employed: an initial review by a senior pathologist followed by a consensus review involving a panel of three specialists. Evaluations indicate a high level of inter-annotator agreement, with a Cohen's kappa score of 0.811. Furthermore, testing demonstrates that the annotations are suitable for training deep learning models capable of accurate polyp classification and dysplasia grading.

This paper addresses information leakage in lossless compression, specifically focusing on the conditional minimum redundancy code (MRC) introduced by Weissman [1]. This code is a specialized form of the minimum redundancy code (MRC) proposed by Gies et al. [2], operating under zero error probability and conditioned on an auxiliary variable. The primary goal is to quantify the conditional mutual information revealed by Weissman code and determine the maximum such leakage. To achieve this, we establish an upper bound expressed through a novel quantity termed the conditional Gies measure, defined as the minimal weighted average edge weight of a specific spanning forest within a constructed weighted directed graph. Furthermore, we propose a tighter upper bound achievable via a greedy algorithmic approach known as the Greedy MRC algorithm. Correspondingly, we also derive lower bounds representing the baseline information leakage. Collectively, these findings offer both an interpretation and practical estimation of information security within zero-error source coding scenarios.

Deep generative models have proven effective across various inverse problem applications, yet their use in Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) super-resolution remains unexplored. This study introduces MrSARP, a hierarchical architecture that integrates both data-driven and problem-specific constraints to synthesize high-resolution SAR imagery from low-resolution inputs. The framework employs two coupled networks: a low-level residual encoder-decoder responsible for extracting local features and performing initial upscaling, and a high-level network that generates global structure to refine the low-level output further. To ensure realistic generation, we incorporate several priors, including specific statistical constraints and a hierarchical hierarchy, alongside a hierarchical loss function to bridge the representation gap between predicted and ground-truth images. Evaluated against multiple datasets, our approach significantly outperforms current methods, achieving a 0.5–1 dB improvement in PSNR and reduced reconstruction errors compared to state-of-the-art techniques.

The quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) represents a hybrid quantum-classical framework designed to tackle combinatorial optimization challenges. In this scheme, quantum resources handle variation exploration while classical computing manages variation tuning; however, classical computing can become a bottleneck due to the costly nature of these parameter tuning processes. This study introduces a Bayesian optimization technique aimed at accelerating the classical side of the QAOA cycle. Our approach utilizes Gaussian processes to build a surrogate model of QAOA variational energy, simultaneously employing an acquisition function to direct the subsequent search. We evaluated our method against standard optimization strategies—specifically grid search, classical gradient-based optimizers, and random search—across several benchmark graphs. Results indicate that our framework achieves a significant speedup in achieving comparable solution qualities.

This paper presents an algorithm for calculating the area of overlap between two ellipses, established by first locating their intersection points and subsequently integrating the resulting boundary functions. Integration is performed using a method that combines elliptic integrals with one or two elementary integrals, taking into account the possibility of up to four real intersection points.

This work examines q-learning within continuous-time Markov decision processes (MDP), specifically addressing the challenges posed by continuous state and action spaces. To address these complexities, we employ cohomology methods to derive uniform convergence rates for the implementation of this algorithm in simulation settings. Furthermore, we analyze the convergence properties of the mean and apply large deviation theory to establish a deviation bound for the algorithm's stochastic fluctuations.

We investigate the low-energy magnetic excitations of half-filled electrons interacting via nearest-neighbor ($V$) and next-nearest-neighbor ($J$) hole-hopping terms within the triangular lattice. Using dynamical mean theory (DMFT) alongside the Bethe-ansatz approach, our calculations reveal a magnetic mode softening as the system approaches the valence bond solid (VBS) transition from the Fermi liquid regime. This finding confirms the existence of such critical softening predicted by VBS theory. Furthermore, we explore an ordered state of fractional occupancy order (FOO) that emerges in the paramagnetic phase due to an effect analogous to order-by-disorders. Our results indicate that this FOO state is most prominent in regimes of strong V and J interactions.

Accurate localization and identification of vertebrae in CT images are vital for spine disease diagnosis and treatment planning, yet this task remains difficult due to the complexity of anatomical structures and image variability. This paper introduces a new framework for automated vertebrae localization and identification, initially utilizing an image rectification method to align and standardize spines across different patients. Following rectification, a fully convolutional network (FCN) trained on a large dataset of manually segmented vertebrae performs segmentation. Crucially, the training of this FCN incorporates a new anatomically-constrained loss function that leverages vertebral spatial relationships to improve robustness and accuracy. Subsequently, an optimization technique based on the constraints derived from vertebral characteristics refines the initial FCN results to achieve precise vertebral identification. Experimental results demonstrate that this framework outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving a mean distance-to-precision (DTP50) of 13.03 mm for vertebral identification and a Dice coefficient of 0.875 for vertebral segmentation.

Within the framework of stochastic thermodynamics, microscopic currents are modeled as integrated activities over specific time intervals. This work establishes that for systems operating in the mesoscopic regime, such as those subject to discrete switching protocols, one can derive a gauge-invariant asymptotic distribution for these fluctuating activities. This distribution serves as a generalized extension of previously proposed asymptotic statistics found in continuous time Markov processes. Furthermore, we examine various applications of this generalized distribution, including analyzing current fluctuations in systems operating under coexisting nonequilibrium conditions and investigating current correlations in environments characterized by temporally fluctuating environments.

This study introduces an innovative approach to acoustic wave control, enabling the  near-100% tunneling transfer of microwaves from one  piezoelectric crystal to another. Achieved through a novel tunnel mechanism, this process allows for waves with wavelengths exceeding 10 times the gap  separation to tunnel across an air  vacuum. This method surpasses the limitations of conventional electrostatic  capacitance coupling in piezoelectric materials. The setup  functions as a tunable device, permitting precise adjustment of both the  switching time and the  switching  ratio for acoustic signals between crystals. This capability holds significant promise for advancing future technologies in  sensing,  actuation, and information processing.

This study introduces an innovative all-optical model reservoir designed for general quantum optics simulations, utilizing exciton-polariton condensates within microcavities. Leveraging fully non-linear Schrödinger equations to describe the dynamics, we demonstrate that this model effectively produces model-state lasers characterized by coherent emission and model-specific statistical properties. Furthermore, we successfully simulate two fundamental model optical components—a model beam splitter and a model mirror—both of which enable the partitioned propagation of model bosonic wavepackets.

The discovery of the ultra-hot gas giant K2-22 b, which orbits its host star in just 33 hours, has generated significant interest due to its extreme atmospheric conditions. Our team utilized the Gran Telescopio Canarias and the Large Binocular Telescope to conduct near-infrared transmission spectroscopy of the system, employing the Large Binocular Interferometer (LBT). This approach offered both exceptionally high spectral resolution and superior angular precision. Our findings indicate that the atmospheric scale height is roughly half of what is predicted by standard models, suggesting the presence of atmospheric haze composed of large particles. Furthermore, our measurements of the measured photo-evaporation-driven mass loss rate are approximately ten times greater than previously reported values. Collectively, our data imply that the atmospheric escape intensity is sufficient to completely strip the planet's hydrogen-rich envelope within a mere 100 million years.

Furthermore, we derive several additional outcomes, including alternate proofs for the Finashin-Fomin Conjecture and the Finiteness Theorem by Finashin and Zaidenberg, as well as precise estimations of the rank for the morphism connecting the first homology groups of the singular fiber to the first homology groups of the ambient space."

This paper introduces Daany, a .NET library designed to streamline data analysis. It offers comprehensive support for mathematical operations, data manipulation, and visualization, making it particularly well-suited for educational purposes. Daany draws inspiration from popular Python packages NumPy and Matplotlib/PYTHON, as well as R's corresponding tools.

Although widely recognized as a titan of the Scientific Revolution, Galileo Galilei's impact on the advancement of mathematics remains surprisingly underappreciated. His mathematical achievements were multifarious, ranging from his early work on motion and the dynamics of falling bodies to his later investigations into the mechanics of the strongest size. His theoretical contributions were matched by significant practical innovations, including the development of the microscope and the telescope, as well as the introduction of the abacus and the Galilean thermometer. His work in these areas helped establish the foundations for the modern disciplines of mechanics, optics, and thermodynamics.

This paper describes a hybrid model designed to simulate the dynamics of magnetic islands, where island centers are governed by a magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) fluid and magnetic field lines are resolved using embedded particle-in-cell (PIC) particles. The approach features adaptive placement of PIC particles within regions of high magnetic gradient, determined by an smoothed particle histogram calculated on an MHD grid. The numerical scheme employs a finite-volume MHD framework combined with a third-order Godunov PIC scheme for collisionless kinetic effects, utilizing a fully-implicit scheme for both time integration and the curl-curl equation. The study numerically investigates the collisionless nature of magnetic island merging, specifically examining how finite Larmor radius effects influence the process. The findings reveal that adaptively embedded PIC particles are vital for capturing kinetic phenomena such as magnetic reconnection and the formation of electron diffusion regions. The results also examine how varying electron Larmor radii impact reconnection rates and the rate at which magnetic island merge.

This paper introduces Ammanuensis, a tool designed to automate the generation of type-safe, functional Rust programs. Its architecture relies on two key components: an extensible query language for accessing a repository of software questions, and a set of programmable answer functions capable of resolving these queries to build program fragments. By synthesizing these parts, the tool creates complete applications. We demonstrate its utility by executing and expanding upon two prior academic prototypes, ultimately concluding with a discussion of its application prospects and future development pathways.
